# TK BF16 FA4 Backward Broad Sweep (2026-07-11)

This report extends the fixed `S=2048,H=2` work in
[the CuTe parity teardown](tk_bf16_bwd_cute_parity_teardown_20260709.md).
Only BF16 backward code and internal backward bindings were exercised.

## Method

- Device: physical GPU 1, NVIDIA GB200,
  `GPU-9d607d77-7203-26c8-e436-2c6747f9b98d`.
- Shape: `B=1, Dqk=192, Dv=128`, BSHD, causal, non-deterministic.
- Each shape used one Q/K/V/dO allocation and one CuTe forward output/LSE.
- Each final row used 8 warmups and 31 CUDA-event samples.
- CuTe, fallback, and split-2 timing calls were rotated by iteration and each
  timed call was synchronized before advancing to reduce route-order bias.
- Times are direct backward-call event times in milliseconds, shown as
  `median [min, max]`.
- `ratio` is TK median / CuTe median. Less than 1.0 is a TK win.

The published `96c4107` binding initially rejected every sequence other than
2048. At `S=512/1024`, both fallback and split-2 first failed the shared
`invalid actual_seq_len` guard. At `S=4096/8192`, fallback ran but split-2
failed its explicit `only wired for seqlen 2048` guard. No unsupported call
was redirected to fallback.

The retained generalization changes only the internal split-2 binding and its
launcher. Existing backward routes keep their `S>=2048` behavior. Split-2 now
requires `S>=512` and `S%512==0`: `S/256` must be even so each KV cluster has
both parity owners, all dense scratch rows are written, and the causal
diagonal/frontier ownership remains unchanged. Scratch allocations were
already keyed by batch, heads, and sequence length.

## Loss Profiles

Bounded torch-profiler timelines explain the crossover.

- `S=2048,H=8`: dQ replay was 87.6 us, dense split dK/dV 133.2 us,
  frontier dK 82.8 us, frontier dV 21.1 us, and merge 7.9 us. dQ and
  dense started first; resource pressure delayed frontier dK until dQ ended,
  leaving a frontier tail. The observed device span was about 264 us.
- `S=4096,H=4`: split instrumentation reported dK/dV 281-284 us, dQ
  179-181 us, and total 313-322 us. dK/dV is the limiting branch.
- `S=8192,H=1`: dK/dV was 261-277 us while the dQ kernel was 312-318 us;
  dQ is the limiting branch and leaves only about 25 us versus CuTe to recover.
- `S=8192,H=4`: profiler durations were dQ 419 us, dense split dK/dV
  627 us, frontier dK 181 us, frontier dV 40 us, and merge 20 us. Resource
  contention delayed dense start to 272 us and frontier start to 727 us;
  total device span was about 973 us versus the 0.444 ms CuTe median.

## Adaptive Long-Sequence Follow-Up

The pushed `a474ef5` checkpoint remained the baseline. All changes below are
internal opt-in backward routes; the default fallback and the published
split-2 binding were not changed.

Dense ownership was generalized from parity to `split_id = cluster_group %
split_count` and `kv_group = cluster_group / split_count`. Non-primary splits
write a packed FP32 allocation whose batch coordinate is `(split_id - 1) * B +
batch`. The merge reads the packed partials in one pass. The cache keeps a
high-water-mark split capacity, so interleaved split-2/split-3/split-4 timing
does not allocate or shrink scratch on route switches.

One dense partial requires
`B*S*H*(Dqk+Dv)*sizeof(float) = B*S*H*1280` bytes. Frontier scratch costs the
same amount independently.

| Shape | One dense partial | split-3 partials | split-4 partials |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S4096 H4 | 20 MiB | 40 MiB | 60 MiB |
| S4096 H8 | 40 MiB | 80 MiB | 120 MiB |
| S8192 H1 | 10 MiB | 20 MiB | 30 MiB |
| S8192 H2 | 20 MiB | 40 MiB | 60 MiB |
| S8192 H4 | 40 MiB | 80 MiB | 120 MiB |

The dense split-2/split-3/split-4 kernels all compile to 168 registers,
198724 B static shared memory, a 64 B stack, and 20/20 B spill stores/loads.
The split-3 merge uses 28 registers with no spills; the measured split-4 merge
used 30 registers with no spills.

All split-count outputs were finite. dK/dV remained in the fallback error

rel L2 `0.00167071`.

Bounded Nsight Systems traces at `S8192,H4` explain why more static splits
lose despite shortening the dense kernel:

| Component | split-2 | split-4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| dense TMEM dK/dV | 620.4 us | 559.7 us |
| dQ replay | 418.0 us | 418.6 us |
| frontier dK | 180.0 us | 121.2 us |
| frontier dV | 40.3 us | 40.5 us |
| merge | 20.5 us | 36.4 us |
| frontier overlap with dense tail | about 169 us | about 18 us |
| device span from preprocess start | about 997 us | about 1042 us |

Split-4 doubles the dense grid from 128 to 256 x-CTAs at this shape. It
finishes dense work about 65 us earlier but prevents the frontier grid from
occupying SMs until the dense tail, then pays 16 us more merge bandwidth.
Split-8 was therefore not justified. A high-priority frontier stream was also
rejected and removed: it stretched dQ from about 423 us to 578 us and left the
graph near 0.984 ms. An integrated masked-frontier dense kernel was finite
(`dK/dV` rel L2 `0.002865/0.001655`) but raised spills to 600/680 B and ran
0.461632 ms versus split-2 at 0.315456 ms. It was removed and the safe route
was rebuilt.

### S8192 H1 dQ Replay Split

At `S8192,H1`, the retained dQ replay launches only 64 CTAs with 215188 B
shared memory per CTA. CTA 0 serially visits up to 128 q-blocks, so the
triangular tail is both load-imbalanced and below full-device CTA count. The
new exact-shape opt-in route assigns two CTAs to each K block and alternates
q-block ownership by `q_block % 2`. The two owners have disjoint q-blocks, so
the existing cross-K TMA add remains sufficient and no dQ merge scratch is
added.

| dQ route | Grid x | Registers | Shared | Stack | Spill stores/loads | Warm dQ kernel |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| retained replay | 64 | 128 | 215188 B | 32 B | 20/28 B | 311-313 us |
| replay split-2 | 128 | 128 | 215188 B | 24 B | 4/4 B | 164-169 us |

dK/dV remains 264-270 us, so the optimized graph becomes dK/dV-bound. The
8-warmup/31-sample result was `0.286624 [0.284096, 0.291904]` ms versus the
retained route at `0.333344 [0.329664, 0.590528]` ms and CuTe at `0.325184
[0.313248, 0.349952]` ms. dQ remains finite but has rel L2 about `0.903`; this
known large dQ error is not fixed by the scheduling change.

## Next Bottleneck

Static multi-split is exhausted for the high-head regime. Split-3 and split-4
reduce per-CTA triangular work, but extra resident dense CTAs suppress frontier
overlap and make the graph slower. The next high-head implementation needs a
bounded persistent work queue or, preferably, a CuTe-like fused main schedule
that owns dense, causal frontier, and dQ accumulation without three competing
grids. `S8192,H2` is still dK/dV-bound after the split-3 improvement. The
`S8192,H1` dQ bottleneck is resolved at the scheduling level; its next limiter
is the same 250-270 us dK/dV branch. At this checkpoint the large dQ numerical
error was still separate correctness debt; the following section resolves it.

## TMEM Superlane Drain Correctness Fix

The large dQ error was a TMEM addressing bug, not an accepted approximation.
`tensor_allocator::allocate<half_tt>(1, col)` starts the second half tile at
physical row 16. A `group<4>::load_async` drains rows `0,16,32,48`, while the
two producer warpgroups use the interleaved full-TMEM mapping. Consequently,
the score, dP, and final dQ drains read the wrong physical rows for half of
the 16-row q subtiles.

The validated fix leaves every MMA producer unchanged. For warp `r=0..3`,
score and dP now use a warp-level `tt_fl<16,64>` view at row `32*r`. The final
dQ reducer does the same for each 64-column chunk of the local and peer
half-tiles, so its effective rows are local `0,32,64,96` and peer
`16,48,80,112`.

Two bounded controls were rejected before retaining the complete fix:

| Probe | S512 H1 dQ rel L2 / max | Repeat behavior | Decision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| final-dQ drain only | 0.975812 / 2.240851 | max repeat delta 0.252954 | rejected; score/dP drains were still corrupt before dS |
| peer MMA destination moved to rows 64-127 | 16.079300 / 22.092773 | max repeat delta 22.132132 | rejected; row 64 is not the legal half-tile superlane destination |
| score+dP+final-dQ `32*r` drains | 0.002734 / 0.006178 | five calls bitwise identical | retained |

`0.131936 [0.117024,0.157920]` ms.

## Long-Sequence TMEM Score/dP Follow-Up

The first post-fix fusion probe tried to reuse dense-main score/dP/dS work for
final dQ. After correcting its TMA descriptor to `__grid_constant__` and
explicitly zeroing the interleaved TMEM destination, dQ was still
nondeterministic and invalid: rel L2 was about `711`, max absolute error was
about `291`, and repeat deltas were hundreds. It also ran about `0.364` ms
versus the retained route near `0.340` ms in the bounded smoke. The probe was
removed completely and the `752cad4` sources were restored before proceeding.

The retained follow-up is narrower. An internal opt-in route replaces the
dense dK/dV kernel's register QK and dO.V products with the already-correct
TMEM score/dP producer. It applies softmax and dS in registers, then feeds the
existing P/dS transpose and dK/dV ownership path. The separate corrected dQ
replay, causal frontier kernels, split ownership, scratch layout, and default
fallback are unchanged. Dense tiles are strictly below the causal diagonal,
so this path intentionally invokes the score/dP producer without masking.

## Standalone TMEM Frontier

The register frontier path launched three dK CTAs per K block, one for each
64-column dK chunk, plus a separate dV CTA. All three dK owners independently
reconstructed QK, P, dP, and dS. The new internal opt-in route uses a
frontier-only specialization of the finite dense TMEM kernel. One clustered
CTA visits exactly the two causal frontier q blocks, applies the diagonal mask
per consumer warpgroup, and accumulates all three dK chunks plus dV in TMEM.
Dense main, dQ replay, scratch ownership, merge, and the default fallback are
unchanged.

The standalone frontier compiles to 168 registers, 199780 B shared memory, a
96 B stack, no local segment, and 48/48 B ptxas spill stores/loads. The removed
register frontier kernels used 228 registers for dK and 231 for dV, with no
shared memory or spills.

## Post-`ee3bd37` Structural Probes

Fresh bounded Nsight Systems captures on physical GPU 1 used identical inputs
and the committed standalone-TMEM-frontier binding. Kernel durations overlap
and therefore do not sum to graph time.

| Shape | TK dense | TK dQ replay | TK frontier | TK merge | CuTe fused main |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S4096 H8 | 270.4 us | 240.5 us | 59.6 us | 20.2 us | 168.3 us |
| S8192 H4 | 475.6 us | 420.2 us | 81.3 us | 20.3 us | 290.5 us |

TK preprocess was `7.1/6.8 us`; CuTe preprocess/postprocess was
`7.6/8.7 us` at S4096 H8 and `7.7/8.9 us` at S8192 H4. The two TK quadratic
grids scale together and each consumes enough shared memory for one CTA per
SM. They compete for residency while independently rebuilding QK, P, dP, and
dS. CuTe's MMA warp instead issues `dQ = dS @ K` from the same per-tile dS,
then reducer warps 0-3 drain 32-column TMEM fragments through TMA reduce-add.
It never exports the dS triangle.

Three bounded implementations tested the handoff boundary. All source and
bindings from these probes were removed after failure, followed by the
explicit backward extension rebuild.

| Probe | Correctness/resource result | S4096 H8 timing | Decision |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| register-transposed KxQ, collective shared store plus shared/shared MMA | dQ unchanged; dK/dV rel L2 `0.730365/0.520246`; REG 168, SHARED 198756 B, spills 28/28 B | `0.441696 ms` vs retained `0.434336 ms` | rejected: shared operand descriptor does not represent the validated TMEM KxQ tile |
| full triangular BF16 dS handoff to standalone dQ consumer | all finite; dQ/dK/dV rel L2 exactly `0.00285756/0.00285128/0.00166185`; consumer REG 255, SHARED 98304 B, no spills | `1.112000 ms` vs retained `0.440832 ms` | rejected: dQ consumer alone was `802.9 us`; O(S^2) reads and FP32 reduce-adds dominate |
| register-transposed KxQ with explicit per-warp K16xQ64 stores | same dK/dV errors `0.730365/0.520246`; REG 168, SHARED 198756 B, spills 28/28 B | `0.443008 ms` vs retained `0.435808 ms` | rejected: correcting producer warp-row ownership does not fix the shared descriptor interpretation |

The final safe rebuild restored the source exactly to `ee3bd37`. A fresh
8-warmup, 31-rotated-sample S4096 H8 control measured CuTe `0.279104 ms`
[`0.267744`,`0.300896`] and TK `0.433856 ms`
[`0.426720`,`0.441344`]. TK dQ/dK/dV rel L2 was
`0.00285756/0.00285128/0.00166185`; all tensors were finite, dK/dV were
bitwise stable over five calls, and dQ repeat max was `1.49e-8`.

The next implementation must keep dS on chip and copy CuTe's ownership, not
its syntax: one bounded dQ TMEM result per q tile, four reducer warps issuing
32-column TMA reduce-adds, and explicit full/empty reuse before score TMEM is
overwritten. For the causal Dqk=192 path CuTe uses one shared dQ reduction
stage, so a full two-stage dS export is unnecessary. The falsifiable gate is a
fused dense+dQ critical path below `300 us` at S8192 H4 with the current
`~0.0029` dQ/dK and `~0.0017` dV error range; otherwise the experiment must
remain unretained.

## S4096 H8 On-Chip Dense dQ Prototype

The opt-in binding
`b300_mha_bwd_hot_cute16_candidate_s4096h8_fused_dense_dq_internal`
implements the bounded ownership above for exactly B1/S4096/H8/Dqk192/Dv128,
causal, non-deterministic BF16 backward. The default fallback and the retained
adaptive route are unchanged. Dense and frontier owners reuse their live BF16
dS tile for one tcgen05 `dQ = dS @ K` result in a dedicated TMEM region. Four
reducer warps wait on both cluster superlanes, load physical TMEM rows
`0,32,64,96` and `16,48,80,112`, add the peers, and issue FP32 TMA reduce-adds.
An empty semaphore prevents score/dP TMEM reuse until all four drains finish.
No global dS materialization or separate dQ replay is used.

The first drain mapped each 64-row group as `[16..63,0..15]`, with norm ratio
1.0 and exact row cosine 1.0. Rotating the destination q subtile by one while
retaining physical row offsets `32*r` fixed the superlane mapping. Moving all
three dQ TMA descriptors into the `__grid_constant__` globals object also
removed an illegal-address failure from by-value descriptor parameters.

### Resources and Critical Path

Ptxas reports 128 registers, 198780 B shared memory, 14 barriers, and a 568 B
frame with 768/920 B spill stores/loads for fused split-2 dense. Fused frontier
uses 128 registers, the same shared memory and barriers, a 384 B frame, and
328/328 B spills. A matched one-call Nsight Systems capture measured dense
`366.1 us`, frontier `86.0 us` (overlapped), merge `22.6 us`, and preprocess
`8.4 us`; CuTe measured main `168.6 us`, postprocess `8.8 us`, and preprocess
`7.8 us`.

Nsight Compute explains why removing the duplicate dQ grid yields only a small
graph win. TK dense launches 512 CTAs of 416 threads and executes 64.43 million
instructions with 602112 local-memory spill requests, 32.8% L1 hit rate,
19.92% achieved occupancy, and 12.75 active warps/SM. CuTe launches 256 CTAs
of 512 threads, executes 22.87 million instructions with 15872 spill requests,
95.07% L1 hit rate, 23.22% occupancy, and 14.86 active warps/SM. TK therefore
still pays twice the CTA count, 2.82x the instructions, and about 38x the spill
requests. The next useful design must reduce compute-role live state and use a
balanced one-cluster-per-key-block scheduler; another dQ handoff alone will
not close the remaining 1.49x gap.

## S4096 H8 Load/Reducer Role Overlap

The exact-shape internal binding
`b300_mha_bwd_hot_cute16_candidate_s4096h8_fused_dense_dq_tail_quarter_load_reducer_internal`
keeps the adaptive-tail ownership above but lets TMA load warp 8 drain dQ
subtile 0 after issuing the next-stage loads. Warps 9-11 drain subtiles 1-3.
This reduces the block from 416 to 384 threads, raising the launch-bounds
register budget without reducing the four-way dQ drain. Existing bindings and
the default remain unchanged.

Moving the reducer base from warps 9-12 to 8-11 changes `warpid()%4` from
`[1,2,3,0]` to `[0,1,2,3]`. Retaining the old `+1` destination rotation gave
a deterministic but wrong dQ with rel-L2 `1.4135`. Removing the rotation only

the split scratch only for the first three quarters of the contiguous B=1

including the default and the high-head control, are unchanged.

## Packed Score FMA Probe (Rejected)

A candidate-local score transform replaced separate score scaling and LSE
subtraction with packed `float2` FMA. The first helper was invalid because it
did not follow TK's row-layout `row_map`: it read the unused
`row_values[i][1]` and assigned packed registers 0/1 to the top row and 2/3
to the bottom row. That build made all three gradients non-finite on every
one of 50 S4096/H8 calls.

The corrected helper reads only `row_values[i][0].x/.y`, replicates each
scalar into a `float2`, and applies the top and bottom values to alternating
`data[k]` and `data[k + 1]` registers for `k += 2`. It was finite over 50
consecutive seed-1 calls at both S4096/H8 and S8192/H4. dK/dV were repeat
stable and dQ repeat max-abs was `2.98e-8`. Relative-L2 versus synchronized
CuTe stayed in the retained range: `0.00284546/0.00283756/0.00165757` at
S4096/H8 and `0.00287989/0.00286266/0.00165860` at S8192/H4 for dQ/dK/dV.

The corrected specialization had the same 168 registers, 199804 B shared,
80 B stack, and 36/44 B spill stores/loads as the retained dS-LDSM route.
Static SASS counts were also identical: 21 FMA, 96 FMUL, 64 FADD, eight
LDSM, and 16 MOVM instructions. Eight warmups and 31 rotated CUDA-event
samples gave:

## P+dS LDSM Dual-Completion Probe (Rejected)

The fused dQ TMEM result aliases both the P columns consumed by dV and the dS
columns consumed by dK. A bounded P+dS `LDSM.MT88` probe therefore attached
independent completion semaphores to dV and the final dK MMA, then waited on
both before issuing dQ into the aliased region. This differed from the prior
single-completion probes by fencing both source regions in the same iteration.

The specialization kept 168 registers, an 80 B stack, and 36/44 B spills. It
removed all 16 MOVM transposes, emitted eight `LDSM.MT88` instructions and
four extra static phase waits, and raised shared memory by 32 B to 199836 B.
Its first synchronized S4096/H8 seed-1 call was finite and exactly matched the
retained route at dQ/dK/dV rel-L2
`0.00284546/0.00283756/0.00165757`. Stability failed: 35 of the following 50
calls produced non-finite dV, while dK remained bitwise stable and dQ repeat
max-abs was `4.47e-8`. The dual completion protocol is therefore insufficient
to make P-side LDSM safe. The flag, semaphores, binding, and probe were removed
without timing, followed by the explicit retained rebuild.

## Two-Stage Fused-dQ TMA Drain

The opt-in internal binding
`b300_mha_bwd_hot_cute16_candidate_high_head_double_buffer_dq_tma_internal`
retains the dS-LDSM score/dP/dS schedule and the S4096/H8 and S8192/H4
guards. It changes only the fused-dQ reducer. The retained path serialized
each 16x64 reduce-add through one shared-memory staging tile. The new path
reuses the P and dS shared regions after both fused-dQ MMAs complete,
alternates 64-column chunks between those two stages, and waits only before a
stage is reused. At most two TMA reduce-add groups are outstanding. No dS is
materialized globally, and existing/default bindings are unchanged.

Fifty synchronized seed-1 calls were finite and repeat stable at both target
shapes. dK/dV were bitwise stable; dQ repeat max-abs was `2.98e-8`. Errors
versus synchronized CuTe were:

### Three-Stage dQ TMA Drain (Rejected)

A follow-up probe removed the remaining `store_async_wait<1>()` before the
third 64-column dQ chunk. The first source-only alias was invalid because the
dS union is exactly one 16 KiB reducer stage at `TileRows=64`; placing another
stage after it crossed into stats/semaphore storage and caused an illegal
access. A corrected opt-in allocated a dedicated 16 KiB third stage.

The corrected specialization was finite and stable over 50 calls at both
S4096/H8 and S8192/H4. Its errors exactly matched the two-stage route, dK/dV
were bitwise stable, and dQ repeat max-abs was `2.98e-8`. It kept 168
registers, 14 barriers, and an 80 B stack, reduced spills from 36/44 B to
28/32 B, and raised static shared memory from 198780 B to 215164 B.

Eight warmups and 31 rotated seed-0 samples rejected it at both shapes:

| Shape | CuTe ms median [min,max] | two-stage ms | three-stage ms | new/control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S4096 H8 | 0.193184 [0.191008,0.317376] | 0.372992 [0.369984,0.405152] | 0.382528 [0.378496,0.560512] | 1.0256 |
| S8192 H4 | 0.314496 [0.311840,0.447360] | 0.604384 [0.601408,0.633856] | 0.616096 [0.614080,5.751776] | 1.0194 |

The final intermediate wait provides useful backpressure; allowing three
outstanding reduce-add groups slows the graph despite lower spills. The
triple-stage flag, storage, binding, and symbols were removed before the safe
rebuild.

### Independent Consumer Barriers (Rejected)

A second schedule probe replaced the two 8-warp consumer barriers around
P/dS staging and TMEM issue with independent 4-warp barriers. The reducer
still waited on both `fused_dq_ready` semaphores. Static resources were
unchanged at 168 registers, 198780 B shared memory, an 80 B stack, and 36/44 B
spills.

The first synchronized S4096/H8 call retained the control dQ/dK errors, but dV
was non-finite. All 50 subsequent calls also produced non-finite dV while dK
remained bitwise stable and dQ varied by at most `2.98e-8`. The cross-consumer
barrier is therefore part of the P-to-dV/shared-tcgen ordering contract, not
removable scheduler overhead. The flag and private binding were removed
without timing, followed by the explicit safe rebuild.

### Pipelined dQ TMEM Loads (Rejected)

A third reducer probe kept the validated two shared stages and TMA
`wait_group<1>` backpressure, but loaded dQ chunks 0 and 1 before one TMEM
wait and overlapped chunk 2's register load with chunk 1's add/TMA issue. The
specialization kept 168 registers, 198780 B shared memory, and an 80 B stack;
ptxas spill stores/loads improved from 36/44 B to 20/24 B for dense main and
from 52/56 B to 28/32 B for frontier.

The initial synchronized S4096/H8 result was finite and exactly matched the
two-stage route and CuTe error metrics. Stability failed: calls 21 and 40 of
the following 50-call same-input stress run produced non-finite output. No
timing was accepted. The result shows that issuing another TMEM register load
before the prior reducer sequence reaches its wait boundary is not safe under
the current shared/tcgen protocol. The flag, explicit drain, and binding were
removed before rebuilding the pushed source.

### Role Register Redistribution (Rejected)

The 384-thread layout has two complete 4-warp compute groups and one complete
load/reducer group, so a CuTe-style conserved `setmaxnreg` probe assigned 200
registers to each compute thread and 104 to each load/reducer thread
(`8*200 + 4*104 == 12*168`). It changed no ownership, shared storage, or
semaphore ordering.

The probe failed the static resource gate. Ptxas still reported 168 registers
but increased dense-main spills from 36/44 B to 912/1164 B and frontier
spills from 52/56 B to 592/624 B. In this monolithic C++ kernel the inline
redistribution point extends live ranges rather than giving ptxas CuTe DSL's
separate role allocation. No smoke or timing was run. The flag, calls, and
binding were removed; a useful setmaxnreg port first requires role code with
explicitly bounded live state.

### Wide 64x128 Score/dP MMA (Rejected)

CuTe's cluster maps both CTAs to one 128-row Q tile and a 256-row K/V owner
tile, whereas the retained TK dense kernel gives each CTA an independent
64-row Q tile. A private probe therefore widened each TK score and dP MMA from
64x64 to 64x128 to reduce the number of score/P/dP/dS loop iterations without
changing split ownership.

The first implementation incorrectly aliased two adjacent `st_bf<64,...>`
objects as one `st_bf<128,...>` descriptor. TK's 128-row shared layout
interleaves swizzle column chunks across all rows, so that alias does not
describe the physical placement of two 64-row objects. It produced dQ/dK
rel-L2 near `0.904/0.902` and intermittent non-finite dV. A corrected probe
explicitly repacked K/V into a true 128-row shared tile and adjusted the
row-half descriptor used by fused dQ. Its first S4096/H8 call recovered the
retained CuTe-relative errors exactly: dQ/dK/dV rel-L2
`0.00284546/0.00283756/0.00165757`.

The corrected route still failed the required 50-call synchronized stress
gate: one S4096/H8 call produced a non-finite output. Static resources were
otherwise unchanged at 168 registers, 198780 B ptxas shared memory, an 80 B
stack, and 36/44 B spill stores/loads. No timing was accepted. The private
binding, descriptor helper, and all source changes were removed before the
explicit safe rebuild.

### Key-Owner-Major Head Interleave (Rejected)

A launch-only probe flattened the dense grid and interleaved heads by owner
slot, preserving every CTA's calculations and all frontier/merge launches.
The falsifiable hypothesis was that grouping the same adaptive owner slot
across heads would reduce the dense tail. Resources were unchanged: 448 CTAs,
384 threads, 168 registers, 198780 B ptxas shared memory, an 80 B stack, and
36/44 B spill stores/loads.

Fifty synchronized calls passed at both target shapes. dK/dV were bitwise
stable, dQ repeat max-abs was at most `2.98e-8`, and the probe exactly matched
the retained route's errors:

| Shape | dQ rel-L2 / max-abs | dK rel-L2 / max-abs | dV rel-L2 / max-abs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S4096 H8 | 0.00284546 / 0.01304626 | 0.00283756 / 0.01172519 | 0.00165757 / 0.01479340 |
| S8192 H4 | 0.00287986 / 0.01225281 | 0.00286264 / 0.01226425 | 0.00165860 / 0.00773048 |

Rotated event samples showed only a small and clock-sensitive apparent gain:
S4096/H8 was `0.371168 ms` versus `0.407744 ms` control in one 31-sample
batch; S8192/H4 was `0.624928 ms` versus `0.643328 ms`, and a 301-sample
repeat measured `0.618624 ms` versus `0.631680 ms`. The matched one-call
Nsight Systems profile falsified the tail hypothesis: dense main was
`565.568 us` interleaved versus `565.760 us` control, while frontier worsened
to `124.416 us` from `98.720 us`. Since the grid order did not reduce the
measured dense critical path, the binding and template flag were removed and
the pushed winner was explicitly rebuilt.

## Isolated BF16 2-CTA MMA Primitive

The retained backward source does not currently exercise a 2-CTA MMA. TK's
generic headers expose `tensor_allocator<...,2>`, `mma2` instruction wrappers,
and cluster completion operations, but the backward path has no validated
leader/peer protocol or 2-SM TMEM fragment abstraction. CuTe's captured
S4096/H8 SASS establishes the target instruction unambiguously: its fused
main contains `UTCHMMA.2CTA` operations.

An isolated `/tmp` PyTorch extension tested the primitive without modifying
repository source. The first probes established three protocol requirements:

1. Both CTAs participate in the 2-CTA TMEM allocation and provide matching
   shared-memory operand offsets, but only cluster rank 0 issues the MMA.
2. Rank 0 commits once with the installed CUTLASS 32-bit cluster-shared
   address form and multicasts to mask `0b11`. Having both CTAs issue the
   multicast hangs; TK's existing 64-bit generic-address helper also hangs.
3. A 2-SM `M=128` accumulator uses a `2x2` TMEM layout that TK's ordinary
   half-tile loader cannot represent. The CuTe-relevant `M=256` score shape
   gives each CTA a standard full `128xN` accumulator. Its eight-warp drain
   order is `[0,2,4,6,1,3,5,7]`, matching TK's full-TMEM load mapping.

The final primitive computes BF16 `A @ B.T` with `M=256`, `N=128`, and
`K=192`: each CTA stages 128 A rows and 64 B rows, while the leader issues the
cluster MMA and both CTAs drain their local 128 output rows. Cuobjdump shows
12 true `UTCHMMA.2CTA` instructions. Ptxas/cuobjdump report 75 registers,
73740/74764 B shared memory, no stack, and no spills.

Against a synchronized torch FP32 reference on physical GPU 1, 50 identical
calls were finite and bitwise stable. Global rel-L2 was `1.99324e-7` and
max-abs was `2.67029e-5`; the four CTA-local 128x64 quadrants were all within
`1.97851e-7` to `2.01806e-7` rel-L2. A 1-CTA control using the same operands
measured `1.96290e-7` rel-L2 and was also bitwise stable.

The dK instruction shape needs one additional constraint. A direct
`M=256,N=192,K=128` wrapper instantiation gives each CTA a 96-row B tile. It
was finite and stable, but only columns `0:96` were accurate; CTA-boundary
swizzling dropped the peer's final 32 rows. Padding B to 128 rows cannot use
the generic wrapper because it derives `N=256` and fails `N == D::cols` at
compile time. A raw explicit-`N=192` descriptor retained the same boundary,
so this was not an instruction-descriptor encoding error.

Decomposing dK into an `N=128` cluster MMA followed by an `N=64` cluster MMA
at TMEM column 128 is correct. Each CTA supplies 64 B rows to the first
instruction and 32 to the second. The isolated kernel emits 16
`UTCHMMA.2CTA` instructions, uses 104 registers and 57356/58380 B shared
memory, and has no stack or spills. Fifty identical calls were finite and
bitwise stable with global rel-L2 `1.40333e-7` and max-abs `1.90735e-5`;
all four CTA-local quadrants were between `1.37413e-7` and `1.42308e-7`
rel-L2.

### M128 dQ 2x2 TMEM Drain

A second isolated `/tmp` extension validated the CuTe dQ instruction shape,
BF16 `A[128,256] @ B[256,192]`, as a true `cta_group::2`
`M=128,N=192,K=256` MMA. Both MN-major shared operands round-tripped exactly,
but TK's generic `tt_fl<16,96>` drain was wrong: it produced rel-L2 `1.21688`
and duplicated or omitted 16-row bands. This isolates the prior failure to the
M128 `2x2` TMEM accumulator drain, not the MMA or shared descriptors.

The drain was derived from CuTe's actual
`make_tmem_copy(Ld32x32bOp(x32), tdQtdQ)` partition and the installed CUTLASS
SM100 copy traits. Four reducer warps map `(Q-row-half,D-half)` to
`(0,0)`, `(32,0)`, `(0,96)`, and `(32,96)`. Their physical TMEM base rows are
`0,32,64,96`; each lane owns one Q row and three 32-column stages. A raw
`tcgen05.ld.sync.aligned.32x32b.x32.b32` drain using that mapping fixed every
CTA and column quadrant.

On physical GPU 1, 50 synchronized calls were finite and bitwise identical.
Global rel-L2 versus torch FP32 was `2.54831e-7` with max-abs `2.67029e-5`;
the two CTA halves were `2.48510e-7` and `2.61075e-7`, and the two 96-column
halves were `2.54739e-7` and `2.54922e-7`. SASS contains 16 true
`UTCHMMA.2CTA` operations and a looped `LDTM.x32`. The lean kernel uses 114
registers, 82956 B shared memory, no stack, and no spills. An earlier debug
build that retained operand round-trip outputs and hoisted all three TMEM
loads used 162 registers; keeping one 32-column fragment live at a time is
therefore a required integration constraint.

The architectural conclusion is now precise: TK exposes
`tensor_allocator<...,2>`, group-2 tcgen05 allocation/commit/sync pieces, and
raw group-2 MMA issue helpers, but the current backward path has no usable
2-CTA MMA abstraction for an M128 `2x2` accumulator. Its generic half-tile
drain applies the wrong physical-row mapping. The isolated instruction and
drain prove the installed toolchain can implement the primitive; production
source remained byte-identical while this was tested.

### Fused On-Chip Tile Microprobe

The next `/tmp` slice validated the missing dS handoff. Each CTA began with
its local `128x128` K-major dS tile, retained its own 64-column Q half, and
bulk-copied the other half through DSMEM into its peer's `K256xQ64` dQ
operand. A debug round-trip of the assembled operand was exact. The lean
handoff plus M128 dQ MMA used 107 registers, 99356 B cuobjdump shared memory,
no stack, and no spills; 50 calls were finite and bitwise stable with dQ
rel-L2 `2.56653e-7` and max-abs `3.43323e-5`.

A final isolated tile then combined all validated pieces in one 2-CTA
kernel: score, P, dP, and dS are computed once for a `K256xQ128` tile; the
same live P/dS feed dV, dK (`N128+N64`), and M128 dQ. Shared storage is
phase-aliased only after dK/dV finish, so dS remains live while retired
K/Q/V/dO/P regions become the dQ operands. No dS is written to global
memory.

The one-contribution kernel emits 60 `UTCHMMA.2CTA` instructions and one
looped `LDTM.x32` dQ drain. Ptxas/cuobjdump report 140 registers,
188492/189516 B shared memory, a 256 B stack, and zero spills. On seed
20260712, 50 calls were finite and bitwise identical with these torch-relative
errors:

| Output | rel-L2 | max-abs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| P | 5.60982e-7 | 1.63913e-7 |
| dS | 1.44446e-7 | 2.98023e-8 |
| dK | 2.26886e-6 | 5.69597e-6 |
| dV | 1.43405e-7 | 1.19209e-7 |
| dQ | 2.29096e-6 | 7.15256e-6 |

Three additional seeds were finite and bitwise stable over 50 calls each.
Their dK/dQ rel-L2 ranged from `7.91e-6` to `1.74e-5`; P remained below
`6.04e-7`. The larger gradient difference is tensor-core/BF16 handoff
rounding and remains orders of magnitude below the prior mapping failures.
With cached output allocations, 200 CUDA-event samples measured `41.376 us`
median (`40.832-64.320 us`) for the single isolated cluster.

A loop-accumulation gate issued a second identical dK/dV contribution with
`mma2_*`. It produced the expected 2x outputs, stayed bitwise stable over 50
calls, retained 140 registers and zero spills, and emitted 84 true 2-CTA
MMAs. Median tile time was `43.360 us`. This validates the accumulator mode
needed for a persistent Q-tile loop; it is not yet a full-sequence timing
claim.

### Integration Plan

The next private long-shape kernel should use the validated shape rather than
incrementally widening the current 64x64 path:

- Map one 2-CTA cluster to a 256-row K/V owner tile and one 128-row Q tile,
  and use an unsplit owner grid. S4096/H8 has 16 owner clusters/head and
  S8192/H4 has 32 owner clusters/head, so both launch 256 dense CTAs instead
  of the retained adaptive split-2 route's 448.
- Stage a real `st_bf<128,192>` K tile per CTA. Two adjacent 64-row objects
  cannot be aliased because their swizzled physical layouts differ.
- Split the 128 Q rows across CTA ranks, issue score and dP only on the leader,
  and multicast completion to both CTAs using the validated 32-bit protocol.
- Keep score/P/dP/dS K-major in each CTA's full 128-row TMEM fragment. This
  removes the retained path's 64x64 shared transpose before dK/dV.
- Issue dK as validated `N=128 + N=64` operations rather than a single
  unsupported per-CTA 96-row B descriptor. dV remains one `N=128` operation.
- Reserve explicit leader MMA and peer relay roles. Accumulate dQ with the
  validated M128 group-2 instruction, then assign four reducer warps to the
  physical rows `0,32,64,96`. Drain one 32-column fragment at a time and issue
  the reduce-add/TMA handoff before loading the next fragment.
- Reuse each live P/dP/dS tile for dK, dV, and dQ before its TMEM region is
  recycled. The falsifiable target is fewer score/dP/dS MMA instructions and
  fewer dense clusters than the 448-CTA 64x64 schedule, while staying near
  the fused microprobe's 140-register/no-spill budget.
- Loop over Q in 128-row steps, using `mm2_*` for the first dK/dV contribution
  and the validated `mma2_*` mode thereafter. Keep the existing causal
  frontier route initially; the new dense loop starts only after the
  256-key-owner frontier so dense and frontier ownership do not overlap.
- Drain dQ with four dedicated reducer warps and the two-stage TMA reduce-add
  handoff already retained by `983e2db`. The raw `LDTM.x32` mapping replaces
  the generic half-tile drain but does not change global dQ accumulation
  semantics.
- Keep the pushed two-stage-TMA winner and existing frontier as controls. The
  first end-to-end route remains private and shape-gated to S4096/H8 and
  S8192/H4 until 50-call correctness and matched timing both pass.

### Private 2-CTA Role-Split Integration

The fused microprobe was integrated behind the existing private
`high_head_cta2_fused_dense_role_split_internal` binding. Default dispatch and
the retained multicast route remain unchanged. The integrated kernel uses 512
threads, reducers 0-3, compute warps 4-11, MMA warp 12, load warp 13, relay
warp 14, and an empty warp 15. It retains reducer-owned V, eight-warp Q/dO
transposes, raw dQ physical rows `0,32,64,96`, and only prefetches the next Q
and dO after the current dK/dV and dQ completions respectively.

The failed next-score lookahead was removed completely. The retained source
contains no `dq_tmem_consumed`, `next_q_ready`, `next_score_count`, or
`early_qdo_prefetch` state. The explicit B200 build reports 128 registers,
230236 B static shared memory, a 312 B frame, and 60/68 B static spill
stores/loads for the original role-split checkpoint.

Fifty synchronized calls on identical CuTe-forward inputs established the
following stable correctness envelope:

| Shape | dQ rel-L2 / max-abs | dK rel-L2 / max-abs | dV rel-L2 / max-abs | Repeat stability |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| S4096 H8 | `0.00313630 / 0.0106964` | `0.00312188 / 0.0103165` | `0.00165615 / 0.0138087` | dK/dV exact; dQ max drift `5.96e-8` |
| S8192 H4 | `0.00312343 / 0.00988495` | `0.00310006 / 0.00726807` | `0.00166733 / 0.0149727` | dK/dV exact; dQ max drift `2.98e-8` |

At S8192/H4, a safe-checkpoint Nsys capture measured `802.848 us` dense,
`236.288 us` frontier, `13.888 us` merge, and `9.120 us` preprocess. NCU
measured 939567 dynamic local-spill requests, only 15.31% cycles with an
eligible warp, 0.15 issued warps/scheduler, and 18.8 long-scoreboard cycles
per issued instruction. The dense kernel, not the already-improved frontier,
is the critical path.

### Role-Split Scheduling Probes

All timings below are rotated CUDA-event medians on physical GPU 1. Absolute
clocks varied substantially, so route/multicast ratios and profiler counters
were used to reject apparent sub-percent wins.

| Probe | Correctness/resources | S4096 H8 | S8192 H4 | Decision |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Move dQ drain from V reducers to compute warps 4-7 | finite, same errors; REG 128, frame 304 B | role `0.413696`, multicast `0.346784` ms | role `0.759808`, multicast `0.601920` ms | rejected: normalized timing neutral |
| Split dV MMA issue to warp 15 while warp 12 issues dK | finite over 50 calls; REG 128, frame 312 B | role `0.452096`, multicast `0.361536` ms | role `0.754208`, multicast `0.601920` ms | rejected: NCU spills `939587`, eligible 15.28%, long scoreboard 19.6 cycles |
| Checkpoint P in BF16 TMEM column 448 | build REG 128, frame 296 B | first smoke illegal access | not run | rejected: tail aliases the live group-2 dQ footprint |
| Reload P from its existing shared tile after dP | finite over 50 calls; REG 128, frame 296 B, static spills 40/40 B | role `0.449152`, multicast `0.390752`, CuTe `0.301888` ms | role `0.763264`, multicast `0.615264`, CuTe `0.416864` ms | retained: role/multicast improves from `1.2645` to `1.2405` at S8192/H4 |
| Compute dS in four 32-column fragments | finite over 50 calls; static spills 40/40 B | role `0.426496`, multicast `0.365056` ms | role `0.813088`, multicast `0.643360` ms | rejected: four TMEM waits erase spill savings |
| Compute dS in two 64-column fragments | finite over 50 calls | role `0.450848`, multicast `0.389984` ms | role `0.797248`, multicast `0.641760` ms | rejected: neutral/slower than full-width shared reload |

The retained shared-P reload replaces compiler-generated local persistence
with one explicit shared load. NCU dynamic local-spill requests fall from
939567 to 600064 (`-36.1%`) while parity is unchanged. The same NCU pass
measured 14.79% eligible cycles and 19.4 long-scoreboard cycles, so local
traffic remains material but is no longer the only limiter. A final Nsys
capture measured `710.784 us` dense, `194.304 us` frontier, `13.472 us`
merge, and `7.328 us` preprocess in that clock window.

Other bounded probes completed before this checkpoint were also removed:

- Starting dK before dV was correct but measured `0.42336 ms` at S4096/H8
  and `0.80701 ms` at S8192/H4, with no normalized win.
- Overlapping the shared copy with dQ reduction produced non-finite gradients
  on the first call.
- Moving Q transpose under dP remained correct but measured `0.456064 ms`
  and `0.806848 ms`; its frame grew to 344 B.
- A global Q-transpose cache was correct but measured `0.823872 ms` at
  S8192/H4. Its copy cost only `27.36 us`, while dense itself regressed to
  `762.272 us`, so it was removed.

The next bottleneck is still structural. The shared-P fix reduces avoidable
local traffic, but TK retains a serial score -> dP -> dK/dV -> dQ tensor-core
chain and a 128-block S8192/H4 grid on a 152-SM device. The rejected split
issuer proves that two producer warps do not overlap the same tensor-core
pipe. A further win requires reducing the live full-width dP/dS work or
changing owner work volume without reintroducing the rejected score lookahead,
early Q/dO prefetch, or dS-in-dead-buffer overlap.

### dS Handoff And Reducer-Owned Q

NCU on the shared-P role-split checkpoint measured `600064` local spilling
requests, 14.98% cycles with an eligible warp, and 19.1 long-scoreboard cycles
per issued instruction. Source correlation showed that the dQ-A shared loads
occurred only after the three dK/dV MMAs completed. The compute warps now load
their local and peer dS fragments before `dkdv_done` and retain them until the
aliased dQ operand storage is available. This does not overwrite shared state
early and does not change the safe next-Q/next-dO prefetch points.

The preload retained the 128-register, 230236-byte shared-memory, 296-byte
frame, and 40/40-byte static-spill profile. Fifty synchronized calls on both
target shapes reproduced the existing finite error envelope exactly. In a
rotated run it measured `0.442272 ms` versus multicast `0.391136 ms` at
S4096/H8, and `0.753184 ms` versus multicast `0.621344 ms` at S8192/H4. The
normalized role/multicast ratios improved from approximately `1.149` and
`1.2405` to `1.131` and `1.2122`. Nsys measured the S8192/H4 dense kernel at
`699.136 us`, down from `710.784 us` in the preceding clock window.

The next role split assigns Q transposition to reducer warps 0-3 after score
completion. Each reducer transposes two logical 16-row Q fragments, with the
existing four-warp source barrier protecting the in-place shared union. dO
transposition and the original eight-compute-warp dK/dV handoff remain
unchanged. This overlaps Q preparation with dP/dS without touching the dQ
semaphore/TMEM protocol.

The Q-only split is finite and stable over 50 synchronized calls at both
S4096/H8 and S8192/H4. Errors remain:

| Shape | dQ rel-L2 / max-abs | dK rel-L2 / max-abs | dV rel-L2 / max-abs | Repeat stability |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| S4096 H8 | `0.00313630 / 0.0106964` | `0.00312188 / 0.0103165` | `0.00165615 / 0.0138087` | dK/dV exact; dQ max drift `5.96e-8` |
| S8192 H4 | `0.00312343 / 0.00988495` | `0.00310006 / 0.00726807` | `0.00166733 / 0.0149727` | dK/dV exact; dQ max drift `2.98e-8` |

The explicit B200 build uses 128 registers and 230236 B shared memory; the
frame falls to 288 B and static spills to 32/32 B. Rotated 51-sample timing
measured:

| Shape | CuTe ms | Retained TK ms | Multicast ms | Role-split ms | Role / multicast |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S4096 H8 | `0.275680` | `0.394784` | `0.388832` | `0.427776` | `1.1003` |
| S8192 H4 | `0.399616` | `0.626080` | `0.641088` | `0.754112` | `1.1763` |

Absolute clocks varied between passes; the same-pass control ratios improved
from `1.131`/`1.2122` to `1.1003`/`1.1763`. S8192/H4 Nsys measured dense at
`670.816 us`, frontier at `193.696 us`, merge at `13.536 us`, and preprocess
at `7.424 us`. NCU local spilling requests fell to `532480`, eligible cycles
rose to 15.40%, and long-scoreboard latency fell to 18.0 cycles. The route is
still private and slower than both retained TK and CuTe, but this role split is
a measured improvement over the prior private checkpoint.

Rejected follow-ups were removed completely:

- Starting next-dO TMA after `dkdv_done` using an explicit eight-warp dS
  preload barrier was correct, but repeated timing was neutral at S4096/H8
  and the S8192/H4 role/multicast ratio regressed from `1.2122` to `1.2217`.
- Moving both Q and dO transposes to reducers and expanding the dK/dV handoff
  to 12 warps preserved dK/dV but corrupted dQ on the first call (`227.409`
  rel-L2, `82.7078` max-abs). The helper, barrier-count change, and dO transfer
  were reverted before the Q-only variant was built.
- Reusing the dead BF16 P register tile for BF16 dS compiled to the same
  128-register, 288-byte-frame, 32/32-byte-spill profile and was timing-neutral;
  the source-only change was removed.

The remaining gap is the serial dP -> dK/dV -> dQ tensor-core chain plus the
full-width dP/dS register traffic. Q preparation is no longer on the compute
critical path, while an analogous dO transfer is unsafe without a separate
completion protocol and has already failed in the combined probe.

### Reducer-Owned dK/dV Output Handoff

Four additional bounded probes followed the `114461c` checkpoint. Moving V
staging ahead of `score_done` corrupted all three gradients on the first call
(`0.9701/0.9813/1.1808` dQ/dK/dV relative L2), proving that the barrier also
protects a live shared/group-2 operand alias. Consolidating 16 score-consumer
arrivals through a local eight-warp barrier was correct over both 50-call
gates, but increased the frame to 296 B and regressed role/multicast to
`1.0992` at S4096/H8 and `1.1738` at S8192/H4. Preloading only one 16x64 dS
half retained the original resources and correctness but measured `1.0700`
and `1.1399`. Finally, backing reducer-owned V with the BF16 TMEM tail at
columns 448-511 compiled but raised an illegal memory access on the first
synchronized call. All four probes were removed.

The retained follow-up moves completed dK/dV output draining from compute
warps 4-11 to reducer warps 0-3. Reducers drain five 32x64 TMEM fragments and
store them cooperatively while compute warps load the second paired owner's K.
A two-arrival cluster barrier delays only the first next-owner dK/dV overwrite;
score and dP can proceed while the prior owner is being written. An explicit
last-`dq_done` wait protects `dq_b` before compute warps replace K. Default
dispatch and the multicast control are unchanged.

The explicit B200 build reports REG 128, a 256 B frame, 231260 B cuobjdump
shared memory, and no local segment. This improves the checkpoint's 288 B
frame at the cost of one 16 B semaphore. Both synchronized 50-call gates
retain the exact error envelope and stability:

### LSE Load Before Score Completion

NCU/SASS correlation on `99d5bf8` identified the largest sampled wait loop as
compute warps blocked on `score_done`. The prior schedule then issued the
global LSE load beside the score-TMEM drain, serializing both dependencies
after that wait. The role-split route now loads only the current tile's LSE
vector before `score_done`. This is a register-only global load: Q, dO,
shared aliases, and MMA issue order are unchanged, so it does not reproduce
the rejected early-Q/dO prefetch.

The build remains REG 128, frame 256 B, shared 231260 B, and no local segment.
Both 50-call gates reproduce the same finite errors and repeat stability as
the reducer-output checkpoint. Two independent 201-sample rotated passes
measured:

| S4096 H8 / 2 | `0.279808` | `0.396832` | `0.388288` | `0.386560` | `0.9955` |

### Rejected Cross-Half Frontier Ownership

A role-only work-volume probe moved the first cross-half dense iteration for
each 256-row owner into rank 0 of the causal frontier. The role kernel then
started at `2 * owner + 2` instead of `2 * owner + 1`, removing one complete
score/dP/dK-dV/dQ iteration per owner. Per-tile and owner-level barrier phases
were kept in separate domains, and the final owner explicitly zeroed its
empty dK/dV output. The resulting kernels passed synchronized first-call and
50-call checks at both target shapes. dK/dV were bit-stable, dQ drift remained
bounded at `5.96e-8` for S4096/H8 and `2.98e-8` for S8192/H4, and all relative
errors stayed in the established envelope.

The role specializations retained REG 128, 256/280 B frames, and 231260 B
shared memory. The extended frontier specialization used REG 168, a 112 B
frame, and 199804 B shared memory. Matched 201-sample timing measured:

`0.00312343/0.00310006/0.00166733` for dQ/dK/dV relative L2. This rules out
shifting a full cross-half tile into the current high-register frontier as a
general long-shape optimization.

### Post-Checkpoint dQ Scaling Probes

Two follow-ups attempted to reduce the new reducer-side scaling cost. First,
the four scalar dQ multiplies per `float4` were replaced by two native SM100
`__fmul2_rn` operations. Resources and all output bits were unchanged, and
both 50-call gates passed. Matched 201-sample medians were
`0.384768/0.388928 ms` role/multicast at S4096/H8 (`0.9893`) and
`0.653600/0.639904 ms` at S8192/H4 (`1.0214`). Nsys measured S8192 dense at
`573.248 us` versus `573.344 us` for the scalar checkpoint, a `0.096 us`
difference inside profiler noise. The explicit packed form was removed rather
than retained as complexity without a measurable win.

The second probe accumulated unscaled dQ from dense main, divided the scaled
frontier contribution back to the same domain, and multiplied final dQ once
inside a role-only dK/dV merge specialization. Its 22-register merge kernel
had no stack or local memory. Both 50-call gates were finite and stable; dK/dV
were unchanged and dQ relative L2 stayed `0.00310772` at S4096/H8 and
`0.00310132` at S8192/H4. The final multiply changed S4096 dQ max-abs by only
`1.19e-7` versus the checkpoint.

The extra global dQ pass nevertheless lost at both shapes:

| Shape | CuTe ms | Retained TK ms | Multicast ms | Late-scale role ms | Role / multicast |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| S8192 H4 | `0.427776` | `0.628320` | `0.641248` | `0.660320` | `1.0297` |

The frontier specialization, merge kernel, template flag, and native-pair
probe were all removed. The exact pushed `6004293` source was restored and
rebuilt with the explicit B200 target.

A final bounded variant moved only dense dK scaling from the reducer output
handoff into a role-only merge kernel computing `dense * scale + frontier`.
This preserved the existing memory pass and operation order. The role kernel
kept REG 128 and 256/280 B frames; the specialized merge used REG 18 with no
stack or local memory. Both 50-call gates passed with checkpoint-equivalent
errors and repeat stability. Matched 201-sample timing was
`0.357632/0.362336 ms` role/multicast at S4096/H8 (`0.9870`) and
`0.633472/0.615072 ms` at S8192/H4 (`1.0299`). The S8192 regression shows the
owner-output multiply is already hidden by reducer output/K-load overlap. The
specialized merge and source changes were removed, followed by an explicit
safe rebuild.

Signaling `owner_output_loaded` immediately after the final dK TMEM load,
before its register-to-global store, was also finite and stable over both
50-call gates with unchanged resources and errors. Matched 201-sample timing
was `0.358016/0.363040 ms` role/multicast at S4096/H8 (`0.9862`) and
`0.629376/0.615968 ms` at S8192/H4 (`1.0218`). These ratios are
indistinguishable from `6004293`, confirming that the last owner store is

and the safe source rebuilt.

### Fresh Long-Shape Profile And Rejected Post-Score dO Copy

Fresh bounded Nsys captures from the pushed `620c4e7` source measured:

| Shape | TK dense us | TK frontier us | TK merge us | TK preprocess us | CuTe main us | CuTe postprocess us | CuTe preprocess us | Dense / CuTe main |

| S8192 H4 | `573.952` | `193.600` | `13.440` | `7.136` | `290.112` | `9.056` | `7.648` | `1.978` |

The target shapes each launch 128 dense CTAs, or 64 two-CTA clusters. This is
only `0.84` cluster waves across the 76 SMs, so the fixed grid underfills the
device while each live cluster remains serialized through score, dP, dK/dV,
and dQ. The roughly fixed 194-195 us frontier is secondary at S8192; the dense
loop accounts for the scaling gap.

A bounded readiness probe split next-Q and next-dO completion again, but unlike
the earlier rejected concurrent-copy version it required `score_done` before
copying dO into the main operand buffer and gated dP on a separate two-CTA dO
barrier. This allowed score to start after Q while intending to overlap the dO
copy only with P exponentiation. REG stayed 128; the specializations used
256/280 B frames, 230268 B shared memory, and zero versus 28/32 B static spills.
The first S4096/H8 call was finite but failed parity badly: dQ/dK/dV relative
L2 was `0.97006/0.98127/1.18083`, with maxima
`2.09742/2.95454/1.17392`. The post-score copy therefore still violates a
shared operand lifetime later in the pipeline. The probe was removed without
timing, the explicit B200 target rebuilt, and the safe checkpoint reproduced
`0.00310772/0.00309447/0.00165615` dQ/dK/dV relative L2.

A second bounded probe moved dQ reducer TMA staging from the main/dQ union
into the dead dS buffer after `dq_done`, then loaded the next Q and dO directly
into their final main-buffer regions. The intended overlap was next score/P
against the previous dQ drain, with the next dS store explicitly waiting for
`dq_reduce_done`. It compiled at REG 128 and unchanged shared memory, but the
S8192 frame grew `280 -> 288 B` and the first S4096/H8 call ended in an
unspecified launch failure. The ownership change was removed at the first-call
gate and the byte-clean pushed source rebuilt. This rules out reusing the
single dS allocation as eight independent TMA-reduce stages without a more
explicit descriptor/alignment and lifetime design.

A score-arithmetic probe multiplied the score-only BF16 K copy by
`scale * log2(e)` once per owner and removed the FP32 multiply from every
score tile; the separate unscaled dQ K copy was unchanged. Resources were
identical, but BF16 operand rounding increased S4096/H8 dQ/dK/dV relative L2
from `0.003108/0.003094/0.001656` to
`0.003765/0.003761/0.002904`. It was rejected at the first-call parity gate
without stress or timing, and FP32 post-MMA scaling was restored.

A final loader-role probe assigned the otherwise empty warp 15 to copy the
prefetched dO tile while warp 13 copied Q, then joined them with a local
two-warp barrier before the unchanged cluster `qdo_ready`. TMA issue points
and all later operand barriers were unchanged. The build retained REG 128 and
256/280 B frames; shared memory increased by one 16 B semaphore. The first
S4096/H8 call was finite but wrong (`0.50093/0.78671/0.95954` dQ/dK/dV
relative L2), showing that the generic two-warp shared-copy handoff does not
preserve the single-loader visibility contract. It was removed without
stress or timing.

### CuTe Wave Comparison And Rejected Buffer/K Reuse

The existing full NCU CuTe S4096/H8 capture launches 256 CTAs in 128
two-CTA clusters, or `1.68` waves/SM. It measures `171.26 us`, 128 registers,
about 223.23 KB dynamic shared memory, 23.22% achieved occupancy, `0.19`
issued and `0.26` eligible warps/scheduler, 22.87M executed instructions, and
15,872 local-spill requests. The current TK launch uses 128 CTAs in 64
clusters (`0.84` waves/SM), 231260 B shared memory, `0.18` issued and `0.22`
eligible warps/scheduler, and 96.42M instructions in the S8192/H4 full NCU
capture. This supports the existing conclusion: TK is limited by one
underfilled wave plus substantially more serial per-cluster work. It does not
justify restoring the already-rejected one-owner grid without first reducing
that work.

Four bounded follow-ups were rejected and fully removed:

| Probe | Static result | First-call result | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Typed `dS`/dQ-reduce shared union plus direct next-Q/dO main loads | REG 128, shared unchanged, S8192 frame `280 -> 288 B` | unspecified launch failure, matching the prior reinterpret-cast attempt | rejected: the overlap has a synchronization/TMA lifetime violation, not just an alignment issue |
| Four single-buffer dQ TMA stages in the peer-qdo union, with peer exchange delayed until `dq_reduce_done` | exact checkpoint resources | finite but dQ rel-L2 `18.10`; dK/dV `0.0658/0.0617` | rejected: the peer region is not a valid independent TMA-reduce-stage layout |
| Skip scale/subtract/exp for the guaranteed-empty causal CTA half | REG 128, but frames grew from `256/280` to `432/424 B` | not run | rejected at static resource gate |
| Load K once and assemble dQ-B through DSMEM | bulk-copy form: frames `304/328 B`; mapped-store form: `304/320 B` | bulk copy preserved dK/dV but dQ rel-L2 was `0.6963`; mapped peer stores raised illegal instruction | rejected: `128x96` raw bytes do not match the `256x96` swizzle, and generic shared stores cannot target the mapped address |

After every rejection, all source edits were removed and the explicit B200
target rebuilt. The final S4096/H8 control again reports finite dQ/dK/dV
relative L2 `0.00310772/0.00309447/0.00165615` with maxima
`0.0106964/0.0103306/0.0138087`. The next structural implementation needs an
explicit CuTe-like multi-stage main allocation or a validated raw DSMEM store
primitive; aliasing current TK tile types cannot supply that pipeline.

### Producer-Published Score And dQ Operands

Before this pass, the proposed two-warp Q/dO staging was compared against the
history above. It was not a materially new protocol: it assigned Q to warp 13
and late dO to warp 15, used the same shared destinations, and joined both
copies at the existing `qdo_ready` publication point. That is the same
dedicated warp-15 late-dO split already rejected at the first-call parity gate,
so it remained fully reverted and was not rebuilt or timed again.

The next score-side probe instead removed the generic group-2 MMA helper's
consumer-side shared-proxy fence for score. All eight K producer warps now
fence before the existing local/cluster K-ready handoff, and the Q/dO loader
fences before the existing two-CTA `qdo_ready` handoff. The MMA warp issues the
same twelve K=16 group-2 BF16 score instructions through a private no-fence
wrapper; tile ownership, instruction descriptors, barriers, and launch order
are unchanged.

The score-only build retained REG 128, 231260 B shared memory, LOCAL 0, and
256/280 B frames for S4096/S8192. Both 50-call gates passed with established
errors, exact dK/dV repeats, and dQ drift bounded by `5.96e-8` and `2.98e-8`.
At S8192/H4, NCU active cycles fell `899838 -> 894822`, duration fell
`976.7 -> 969.5 us`, warp cycles per issued instruction fell `20.42 -> 20.32`,
and executed instructions fell `96.42M -> 96.37M`. Nsys dense main fell from
the checkpoint `573.344 us` to `570.912 us`. Matched score-only timing was:

### Rejected Normal-Layout dK Operand

A bounded role-only probe removed the reducer-side Q register transpose and
stored the gathered Q fragments in normal layout, then changed the two dK
group-2 instructions from ABt to AB. It was rebuilt before validation and
passed the first-call and both 50-call finite/stability gates. The different
register-tile shape nevertheless increased the role specialization stack
frames from `256/280 B` to `272/288 B`. Matched normalized timing regressed to
role/control `1.0007` at S4096/H8 and `1.0342` at S8192/H4, so eliminating the
transpose did not repay its extra live-state and spill cost. The helper,
normal-layout shared writes, and AB dK instructions were removed. A forced
B200 rebuild restored the pushed `64b85f3` kernel byte-for-byte at REG 128,
231260 B shared memory, LOCAL 0, and `256/280 B` frames. No result observed
before a completed explicit build is included here.

### Shape-Gated TMEM-A dV/dK

CuTe's 2-CTA Dqk192/Dv128 layout packs S/P at TMEM column 320 and dP/dS at
384, then consumes P and dS as TMEM-A operands. A bounded role-route probe
ported that ownership without changing Q/dO staging, dQ exchange, frontier,
or either control route. SASS showed the intended true 2-CTA
`UTCHMMA.2CTA tmem[...], gdesc[...]` forms.

The first complete port exposed one mapping restriction. Direct TMEM-A dV
was correct, but reloading packed BF16 P from TMEM into the generic TK
`group<8>` register tile made dS, dK, and dQ non-finite. Adding explicit
score/dP load-completion barriers did not change that signature and raised
the specialization frames to `320/264 B`. Keeping dK on shared A also did not
help while dS still used the packed P reload. These variants were rejected at
the first-call gate without timing.

Restoring the validated shared P reload made dS finite while retaining a
second packed P copy for TMEM-A dV. The same correction proved that dS TMEM-A
for dK was independently valid. Both 50-call gates then reproduced the
checkpoint error envelope exactly, with exact dK/dV repeats and dQ drift of
at most `5.96e-8` at S4096/H8 and `2.98e-8` at S8192/H4. Applying the TMEM-A
path to both specializations measured role/multicast `0.9795` at S4096/H8 but
`1.0314` at S8192/H4. A dV-only slice was weaker at `0.9875/1.0397`.

The retained implementation therefore gates packed P plus disjoint dP/dS
TMEM and TMEM-A dV/dK to `PreloadDpsum=false`, the S4096 specialization.
`PreloadDpsum=true`, used by S8192, compiles the exact pushed shared path.
Final resources are REG 128, 231260 B shared memory, LOCAL 0, and `256/280 B`
frames for S4096/S8192 respectively. Final serial validation from the rebuilt
artifact was:

| Shape | dQ rel-L2 / max-abs | dK rel-L2 / max-abs | dV rel-L2 / max-abs | 50-call stability |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| S4096 H8 | `0.00310772 / 0.0106964` | `0.00309447 / 0.0103306` | `0.00165615 / 0.0138087` | dK/dV exact; dQ max drift `5.96e-8` |
| S8192 H4 | `0.00310132 / 0.00988495` | `0.00308147 / 0.00779080` | `0.00166733 / 0.0149727` | dK/dV exact; dQ max drift `2.98e-8` |

Matched rotated timing from the final shape-gated artifact measured:

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

A bounded S4096/H8 Nsys capture measured dense/frontier/merge/preprocess at

A post-checkpoint S8192-only follow-up stored dS in the existing TMEM 384
alias and used TMEM-A only for dK, while leaving P, dP, and dV on the pushed
shared path. It retained REG 128, 231260 B shared memory, and the 280 B frame,

## S8192/S16384 Role-Split Generalization

The private role-split route was generalized without changing its kernel
dataflow or any default dispatch. The opt-in guard now accepts S8192 and
S16384 with H4/H8/H16, while S4096 remains restricted to the published H8
cell. S16384 uses the existing paired ownership (`owner_idx`, reflected
`owner_idx`) and the same `PreloadDpsum=true` specialization as S8192.
Resources are unchanged at REG 128, 231260 B shared memory, LOCAL 0, and a
280 B frame with 28/32 B static spill stores/loads.

Every new cell passed a synchronized 50-call gate. dK and dV were bit-exact
across repeats; dQ maximum repeat drift was at most `5.96e-8`. The error
range across S8192/S16384 H4/H8/H16 was dQ rel-L2
`0.003101-0.003148`, dK `0.003081-0.003147`, and dV
`0.001655-0.001663`. Representative per-cell matched errors and isolated

The role route is a reproducible `2.30-2.60x` improvement over fallback on
these cells and repairs the missing fast-route coverage, but it does not
close the CuTe gap. Raising heads falsifies the hypothesis that the S8192/H4
loss is primarily the `0.84`-wave launch: role/CuTe worsens at H8/H16 even
though the larger grid supplies more waves. The serial per-cluster pipeline
and shared traffic dominate once occupancy is available.

A one-process H16 -> H4 -> H16 transition probe found separate correctness
debt in the fallback route. The role route reproduced itself with dQ drift
`2.24e-8` and unchanged dK/dV, while fallback dQ changed by rel-L2 `13.86`
and max `37.18`. CuTe dQ changed only `1.91e-6`. Broad timings above therefore
use isolated bounded processes per shape; the fallback transition result is
not attributed to the generalized role kernel.

At S16384/H8 the same split becomes more pronounced: TK
dense/frontier/merge/preprocess is
`4383.872/232.800/70.080/23.584 us`, while CuTe
main/postprocess/preprocess is `1511.232/39.616/24.992 us`. Frontier is only
4.9% of TK kernel time; dense main is 93.1%. The remaining target is therefore
the score -> dP -> dK/dV -> dQ group-2 MMA pipeline and its shared operand
traffic, not frontier, preprocessing, or launch order.

One CuTe-layout probe gave score and dP distinct TMEM destinations (columns
320 and 384), issued dP immediately after score commit, and waited for score
consumption before later reuse. It was resource-neutral but failed the first
call: dQ/dK/dV rel-L2 became `0.14855/0.14835/0.13582`. A distinct TMEM
column does not make a score TMEM read safe while the next group-2 MMA is
queued under the current protocol. The binding, template, and all source
edits were removed; the explicit safe rebuild reproduced the retained route.

A subsequent direct-TMEM dQ probe reinterpreted the packed dS accumulator as
the A operand of a group-2 `dQ = dS @ K` MMA and removed the register/shared
dS handoff. The resulting SASS contained the intended true TMEM-A
`UTCHMMA.2CTA` form and remained resource-neutral at REG 128, 231260 B shared
memory, LOCAL 0, and a 280 B frame. It failed the first synchronized S8192/H4
call: dQ contained NaNs, while dK and dV remained finite and retained rel-L2
`0.00308147` and `0.00166733`. The failure is structural rather than a row-map
micro-error: the existing dS accumulator occupies TMEM columns 384-511, while
the current dQ C tile occupies columns 320-511, so the queued MMA aliases its
A and C regions. The private binding and all source edits were removed.

The explicit safe rebuild completed at `2026-07-13 01:03:41 UTC`. Resource
metadata returned to the retained `<false>/<true>` role kernels at REG 128,
STACK 256/280, SHARED 231260, LOCAL 0. Post-build 50-call gates passed at
S4096/H8 and S8192/H4: dK/dV were bit-exact, dQ maximum drift was
`5.96e-8`/`2.98e-8`, and dQ/dK/dV rel-L2 was
`0.003108/0.003094/0.001656` and `0.003101/0.003081/0.001667`, respectively.

### Retained dS Exchange Half

CuTe's BF16 compute loop retains the dS half destined for the peer CTA in
registers while publishing the other half to shared memory. A first TK port
also stored dS to TMEM for dK. After correcting the producer-row mapping from
physical `compute_warp` to logical `output_subtile`, it was finite and stable,
but only changed S8192/H4 role timing from `0.650112` to `0.647488 ms` and
still lost to the retained controls. The extra full dS TMEM store canceled
most of the saved shared transfer, so that version was removed.

The retained private specialization keeps shared dS and the existing dK MMA,
but carries only the peer's 64-column dS half in registers across dK/dV. The
local half follows the original shared reload; the retained half is written
directly to the exchange buffer at its logical output row. This removes one
16 KB shared load per CTA and dense iteration without changing MMA order,
frontier ownership, default dispatch, or the original role binding. The new
binding is restricted to S8192 H4/H8/H16 and S16384 H8/H16.

and dV were bit-exact across repeats; dQ maximum repeat drift was at most

### Rejected Reducer dO / Early dV Pipeline

A private H8-only probe gave P and dP disjoint TMEM regions, had reducer warps
gather dO into the validated normal dV layout only after `dp_done`, and issued
dV while compute warps formed dS. It did not prefetch or overwrite dO while
dP was live. The first barrier-reuse version hung; explicit private barriers
made one call correct, but 50 calls exposed non-finite dV because the dV
barrier did not cover all eight P-to-TMEM producers. Adding the missing
eight-warp P completion edge fixed the race.

The corrected specialization used REG 128, STACK 264 B, SHARED 231308, and
LOCAL 0. Both 50-call gates then reproduced the both-half error envelope:
S8192/H8 dQ/dK/dV rel-L2 was
`0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733`, and S16384/H8 was
`0.00313664/0.00312595/0.00166289`. dK/dV were exact across repeats; dQ drift
was `5.96e-8` and `2.98e-8` respectively.

The extra P TMEM store, normal-dO gather, and producer barriers cost more than
the dV/dS overlap saved. Isolated 201-sample medians were CuTe/both/probe
`0.604832/1.264064/1.290272 ms` at S8192/H8 and
`1.659776/4.447424/4.548448 ms` at S16384/H8. Nsys measured S8192 dense main
at `1140.288 us` versus the both-half checkpoint's `1116.896 us`. The private
binding, template flag, semaphores, and all dataflow edits were removed. The
three backward sources byte-match `bf6bf53`, followed by an explicit safe
B200 rebuild.
