### Rejected Persistent-V And Early V-Staging Probes

Source inspection after the normal-dV checkpoint found another difference
from CuTe's D192 path. TK aliases the reducer-owned V tile and per-iteration
dS in `storage.ds`, so all four reducer warps rewrite V after every score.
CuTe keeps P/dS in TMEM and does not require that V restage. A private H8
probe therefore kept V resident for the full owner, issued dV through a
dedicated ready/done edge while compute warps formed dS, and reused the dead P
shared tile for dS and dK. It retained the true two-CTA MMA path at REG 128,
STACK 256 B, SHARED 231308 B, and LOCAL 0.

Two initial handoff placements exposed the exact shared aliases. Staging the
next dO in `storage.ds` overwrote persistent V and produced dQ/dK rel-L2 near
`0.75` while dV remained correct. Staging it in `main.p` after `dq_done`
overwrote the union's live dQ reduce stages; waiting for all reducers instead
formed a completion cycle. Both placements were removed. The corrected
version staged next dO in `qdo_phase` after dQ consumed peer dS, copied it out
before the next peer-Q/dO load, and then reused that union normally.

The corrected route passed both 50-call gates. At S8192/H8, dQ/dK/dV rel-L2
was `0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733`; at S16384/H8 it was
`0.00313664/0.00312595/0.00166289`. dK/dV were bit-exact and maximum dQ drift
was `5.96e-8`/`2.98e-8`. It nevertheless failed the first performance gate:
an isolated 201-sample S8192/H8 pass measured CuTe/normal-dV/persistent-V at
`0.604960/1.180288/1.227744 ms`, so persistent V was `1.0402x` the parent.
Matched Nsys placed the entire regression in dense main:
`1156.480 us` versus `1103.872 us`; frontier remained
`213.024` versus `212.032 us`. The extra dV completion and qdo-phase handoff
cost more than the removed V stores, so the binding and all source edits were
removed.

A smaller follow-up moved the unchanged V store and its existing operand
arrival before `score_done`, without moving Q/dO reads or changing any later
buffer lifetime. It was resource-neutral at REG 128, STACK 256 B,
SHARED 231260 B, and LOCAL 0, but failed the first S8192/H8 call with
dQ/dK/dV rel-L2 `1.0283/1.0387/1.6220`. This proves the current score edge
also protects a shared operand reuse not represented by the local V barrier.
The probe was removed without timing. An explicit B200 rebuild restored the
three backward sources byte-for-byte to `01257fc`.

### Rejected TMA Operand Staging

Two H8-only probes tested whether replacing distributed register/shared
operand staging with one TMA transaction could reduce the remaining shared
LSU volume. Both preserved the score/dP/dK-dV/dQ order and were removed after
failing the timing gate.

The first replaced the four reducer-warp V loads and shared stores with one
post-score `128x128` V TMA load. It was finite over 50 calls at S8192/H8 and
S16384/H8: dK/dV were bit-exact, dQ drift was at most `5.96e-8`/`2.98e-8`,
and dQ/dK/dV rel-L2 remained
`0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733` and
`0.00313664/0.00312595/0.00166289`. The kernel used REG 128, STACK 256 B,
SHARED 231276 B, and LOCAL 0. An isolated S8192/H8 201-sample pass measured
CuTe/normal-dV/TMA-V at `0.598784/1.180256/1.249472 ms`; the single TMA and
completion edge regressed the parent by `5.86%`.

The second removed the peer-dO exchange and eight-compute-warp normal-layout
dO gather. After `dp_done`, the loader issued one `128x64` dO TMA per CTA
directly into the existing normal dV operand view while compute warps formed
dS. This is later than the previously rejected early-dO probes and does not
overwrite dO while dP is live. It passed both 50-call gates with the same
errors and repeat stability as normal-dV. Resources were REG 128, STACK 272 B,
SHARED 231276 B, and LOCAL 0. Matched 201-sample medians were:

| Shape | CuTe ms | normal-dV ms | direct-dO-TMA ms | direct/normal |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S8192 H8 | `0.604512` | `1.184672` | `1.188960` | `1.0036` |
| S16384 H8 | `1.653344` | `4.412960` | `4.429344` | `1.0037` |

The distributed normal-dO gather is already hidden well enough that the TMA
completion and larger frame cost more than the removed shared instructions.
Both private bindings, descriptor additions, semaphores, and template flags
were removed. The explicit safe B200 rebuild completed with all three
backward source files byte-identical to `01257fc`.

A third score-side mapping probe revisited the previously non-finite packed-P
reload with explicit role-kernel ownership. Compute warp `r` stored and
reloaded its `16x128` BF16 P fragment at TMEM physical row
`16 * output_subtile(r)` and dP used the disjoint column-384 accumulator.
Shared P and the validated dV path remained unchanged to isolate the
roundtrip. The specialization was resource-neutral at REG 128, STACK 256 B,
SHARED 231260 B, and LOCAL 0, but its first S8192/H8 call made dK and dQ
non-finite while dV exactly retained its normal error. An explicit eight-warp
score-load completion barrier before the mapped P store produced the same
signature. This rules out only a missing producer barrier: TK's packed BF16
TMEM register representation still does not match the role kernel's P
fragment layout. The private route and all source edits were removed, and the
safe B200 artifact was rebuilt from byte-clean backward sources.

A final shared-LSU probe replaced the local/peer shared dO source loads with
eight distributed `16x64` global loads at the unchanged late normal-dV gather
point. It kept the peer-dO TMA and all barriers for this first isolation, so
it changed only the source of each compute warp's dO register fragment. The
route used REG 128, STACK 264 B, SHARED 231260 B, and LOCAL 0. Both 50-call
gates passed with the normal-dV error envelope, exact dK/dV repeats, and dQ
drift bounded by `5.96e-8`/`2.98e-8` at S8192/S16384 H8.

The added long-scoreboard exposure outweighed the shared-load removal.
Matched 201-sample medians were CuTe/normal/global-dO
`0.608736/1.255456/1.274368 ms` at S8192/H8 and
`1.676672/4.429568/4.770784 ms` at S16384/H8. The candidate regressed the
parent by `1.51%` and `7.70%`, respectively, so it was removed and the
byte-clean normal-dV artifact rebuilt. Together with the direct-dO TMA result,
this shows that the current shared dO gather is not the next useful target;
the remaining work must change score/P/dS TMEM ownership or tensor issue
utilization without adding a new memory-latency dependency.

### Rejected CuTe-Tail And Staged-Q Probes

CuTe source inspection clarified the D192 BF16 TMEM contract. Its two-CTA
layout places dS at column 384 and the dQ accumulator at
`512 - Dqk/2 = 416`. Relocating only TK's dQ accumulator from column 320 to
416 was finite and matched the normal-dV control: dQ/dK/dV relative L2 stayed
`0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733`, and candidate/control dQ quadrant
differences were `2.5e-8` to `3.1e-8` relative L2. The specialization used
REG 128, STACK 256 B, SHARED 231260 B, and LOCAL 0. This proves that the CuTe
tail address is legal in TK, but placement alone removes no work and was not
retained.

A follow-up reinterpreted a packed dS TMEM store as the dQ TMEM-A operand.
SASS showed the intended true TMEM-A `UTCHMMA.2CTA`; resources were REG 128,
STACK 272 B, SHARED 231260 B, LOCAL 0, with 28/44 B static spill
stores/loads. Generic group-8 dS storage was finite but produced dQ relative
L2 `0.76578`; explicit logical rows `16 * output_subtile` produced `0.81844`.
dK and dV remained at `0.00311643/0.00165733`. CuTe source establishes why
this is not the BF16 parity path: BF16 dQ consumes shared dS (`sdS`), while
TMEM dS is the dK operand; the CuTe R2T packed layout is not represented by
TK's generic register-tile store. The probe was removed without timing.

A separate private H8 probe attempted to overlap the local Q copy with score.
For iterations after the prologue, score consumed the completed `next_q`
stage directly and a new local barrier published its copy into `main.q` for
the later reducer-owned dK transpose. The first form copied concurrently with
score; it failed because both views share the phase union. A corrected form
waited for `score_done` before the copy, but the staged descriptor still was
not equivalent to the validated score operand. Its first S8192/H8 call was
finite but wrong: dQ/dK/dV relative L2 was
`0.53792/0.96350/1.33780`. The route used REG 128, STACK 256 B, SHARED
231276 B, and no static spills. Both forms, their binding, and the extra
semaphore were removed at the first-call gate; no timing was accepted.

The explicit safe B200 rebuild then restored all three backward source files
byte-for-byte to `e8d33fa`. Post-build 50-call controls passed at S8192/H8
and S16384/H16. Their dQ/dK/dV relative L2 values were
`0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733` and
`0.00313920/0.00312162/0.00165859`; dK/dV were bit-exact and maximum dQ
repeat drift was `5.96e-8` on both shapes.

A final generalization probe instantiated the validated normal-dV/both-half
template at S4096/H8 behind a new private binding. It passed 50 calls with
the role-control dQ/dK/dV relative L2 values
`0.00310772/0.00309447/0.00165615`; dK/dV were bit-exact and dQ drift was
`5.96e-8`. Resources remained REG 128, STACK 256 B, SHARED 231260 B, and
LOCAL 0. Timing was not reproducible: the first rotated 201-sample process
measured CuTe/role/normal-dV at `0.309920/0.358016/0.347616 ms`, while the
second measured `0.298880/0.354048/0.371840 ms`. Because one pass regressed
role by 5.0%, the S4096 guard and binding were removed and were not promoted.

### H16 Scaling And Rejected Normal-dV TMEM-P

Matched one-call S8192/H16 Nsys captures make the remaining scaling gap
explicit. The retained normal-dV graph spent `2200.256 us` in dense main,
`221.024 us` in frontier, `69.920 us` in merge, and `24.416 us` in
preprocess. CuTe spent `844.064 us` in its fused main, `39.424 us` in
postprocess, and `25.152 us` in preprocess. TK launched a `32x16` CTA grid,
or 256 two-CTA clusters, while CuTe launched `64x16`, or 512 clusters. Since
both launches supply multiple waves, TK's `2.61x` dense-main loss is not a
global underfill explanation.

A bounded matched NCU counter pass confirms a per-tile instruction and
shared-traffic gap. Values below are TK normal-dV/CuTe:

| Counter | TK | CuTe | TK/CuTe |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Executed warp instructions | `389.758 M` | `170.639 M` | `2.28x` |
| Shared load wavefronts | `38.223 M` | `19.241 M` | `1.99x` |
| Shared store wavefronts | `74.495 M` | `22.609 M` | `3.29x` |
| DRAM bytes | `553.94 MB` | `407.57 MB` | `1.36x` |
| Tensor-pipe active | `20.23%` | `52.30%` | `0.39x` |
| Long-scoreboard stall | `73.37%` | `61.99%` | `1.18x` |
| Eligible warps/scheduler | `0.24` | `0.27` | `0.89x` |

The next private probe combined two pieces that had not previously been
tested together: the retained normal-layout dO operand and CuTe-like packed
P ownership. Compute warps kept P in registers for dS, stored P in its
column-320 TMEM slot, moved dP to the disjoint column-384 slot, and issued dV
with TMEM P plus normal shared dO. This removed the shared P store/reload from
the iteration without changing score, dK, dQ, frontier, or owner scheduling.
SASS retained true `UTCHMMA.2CTA` and used the intended TMEM-A dV form.

The route was correct over 50 synchronized calls at S8192/H8 and
S16384/H16. Their dQ/dK/dV relative L2 values were respectively
`0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733` and
`0.00313919/0.00312162/0.00165859`; dK/dV were bit-exact and maximum dQ
repeat drift was `5.96e-8`. Retaining P across dP nevertheless changed the
normal-dV resource profile from REG 128, STACK 256 B, no spills to REG 128,
STACK 272 B with 20/32 B spill stores/loads. Two isolated 201-sample
S8192/H8 passes measured CuTe/normal-dV/probe at
`0.604416/1.183872/1.249856 ms` and
`0.598656/1.183424/1.248160 ms`. The probe regressed normal-dV by
`5.57%/5.47%`, so it was removed completely.

The explicit safe B200 rebuild completed at `2026-07-13 04:55:55 UTC` from
byte-clean backward sources. The retained normal-dV binding loads and the
failed TMEM-P symbol is absent. This falsifies shared-P removal through
full-tile register retention; a useful follow-up needs a correctly mapped
short-lived TMEM P drain or a score-side work reduction without extending P's
live range.

Source-correlated NCU attributed about `7.08 M` dynamic warp instructions at
S8192/H8 to `cta2_role_split_select_ds_half`, which copies the two dS halves
retained for the late dQ MMA. A private probe replaced both copies with direct
half-width BF16 conversion from `ds_reg`. It passed 50 synchronized calls at
S8192/H8 and S16384/H16 with the normal-dV error envelope: dQ/dK/dV relative
L2 was `0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733` and
`0.00313919/0.00312162/0.00165859`; dK/dV were bit-exact and maximum dQ drift
was `5.96e-8`. The changed conversion shape raised resources from REG 128,
STACK 256 B with no spills to REG 128, STACK 272 B with 20/32 B spill
stores/loads. Two isolated 201-sample S8192/H8 passes measured candidate versus
normal-dV at `1.203424/1.183296 ms` and `1.203040/1.183296 ms`, regressions of
`1.70%` and `1.67%`. Reusing the existing preload variable names increased
spills further to 28/44 B and was rejected at the static gate. Both forms and
their private binding were removed. The explicit safe B200 rebuild completed
at `2026-07-13 05:12:50 UTC`; a fresh S8192/H8 50-call control retained finite
outputs, dK/dV bitwise stability, `5.96e-8` maximum dQ drift, and the expected
`0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733` relative-L2 errors.

A follow-up avoided the alternate half-width conversion entirely: it retained
the existing full `rt_bf<16,128>` dS conversion across dK/dV and referenced its
two contiguous `rt_bf<16,64>` halves only at the late dQ operand stores. This
would remove both selection copies without changing the conversion shape or
the dS shared store. The specialization compiled at REG 128 and SHARED 231260
B, but its stack frame grew from 256 B to 400 B. It was rejected at the static
resource gate without correctness or timing, fully removed, and the explicit
safe B200 artifact rebuilt from byte-clean backward sources. Retaining either
the full dS tile or a separately converted pair therefore extends live state;
eliminating this helper requires a shorter producer-consumer lifetime rather
than another register representation.

A CuTe-layout hybrid then published P to both the existing shared tile and
TMEM column 320, moved dP to column 384, kept shared P for dS, and consumed
TMEM P with the retained normal-layout dO for dV. Unlike the earlier
register-retained TMEM-P probe, this did not extend P's register lifetime.
The immediate-completion form was resource-neutral at REG 128, STACK 256 B,
SHARED 231260 B, and LOCAL 0; SASS showed the intended TMEM-A
`UTCHMMA.2CTA`. It passed 50 calls at S8192/H8 and S16384/H8 with the
normal-dV errors and repeat stability. Two isolated S8192/H8 201-sample
passes nevertheless measured hybrid/normal at `1.241344/1.183968 ms` and
`1.241920/1.183552 ms`, reproducible regressions of about `4.9%`. Matched
Nsys placed the loss entirely in dense main: `1167.328` versus `1106.496 us`,
with frontier flat near `212 us`.

Deferring `tcgen05.wait::st` until after dP/dS reduced the loss but raised the
frame to 264 B and still measured `1.217824/1.184352 ms` (`+2.83%`). Replacing
that wait with the documented `fence::before_thread_sync`, existing operand
barrier, and `fence::after_thread_sync` handoff also passed 50 calls but
measured `1.291648/1.257024 ms` (`+2.75%`) in its clock window. All three
forms were removed and the explicit safe B200 artifact rebuilt at
`2026-07-13 05:44:51 UTC`. A second full P publication is therefore not the
path to CuTe parity even when its completion overlaps useful work.

### TMA Score-K Owner Publication

A new private specialization replaced only the once-per-owner score-K
publication. In the retained normal-dV route, the eight compute warps each
loaded a K fragment from global memory and stored it into the clustered score
operand. The new route has the loader warp issue one TMA load into the same
shared K tile while the compute warps build the unchanged dQ K layout, then
publishes the existing cluster `k_ready` barrier. Iteration ownership, dP/dS,
dK/dV/dQ, frontier, and default dispatch are unchanged.

The S8192/H8 and S16384/H8 50-call gates passed with dQ/dK/dV relative L2
`0.00312103/0.00311643/0.00165733` and
`0.00313664/0.00312595/0.00166289`. The widened H16 guard also passed 50 calls:

errors matched the normal-dV control. `cuobjdump` reports REG 128, STACK 256 B,
SHARED 231260 B, and LOCAL 0, exactly matching the normal-dV control with no
spills. The final implementation reuses the mutually exclusive
`k_local_ready` semaphore for TMA completion and compile-guards the K
descriptor prefetch, so the control specialization is resource- and
instruction-clean.

An isolated follow-up tried to hide the second owner's score-K TMA. After the

### Dead-P dQ Drain And Direct Next Q/dO

The next private specialization changes the per-iteration shared-memory
handoff without moving an operand before its validated completion. After dV,
dK, and dQ MMA completion, the two exact `st_fl<32,32>[2][4]` reducer stages
are placed in the now-dead 32 KiB shared-P allocation. This leaves the Q and
dO regions disjoint, so the loader issues the next tile's existing Q and dO
TMA descriptors directly into their final main-loop destinations while the
previous dQ is drained. The following iteration waits for the same byte-counted
TMA barrier but no longer copies 40 KiB through one loader warp. The score,
dP, dK/dV, dQ MMA, peer exchange, owner pairing, frontier, and default route
are unchanged. This differs from the rejected dS-buffer probe: no reducer
stage is reinterpreted in `storage.ds`, and the exact typed reducer object is
statically checked to fit the dead P allocation.

### Direct Statistics LDS Mapping and Dense/Frontier Race Fix

The split-LSE route still used TK's generic warp row-vector loader for the
shared LSE and dPsum stages. A private B1/S16384/H8 probe replaced only those
loads with the physical `rt_fl` mapping: for fragment `f` and lane pair
`lane & 3`, each warp loads rows `16*f + 2*pair + {0,1}` and
`16*f + 8 + 2*pair + {0,1}`. The score scaling, direct approximate base-2
exponentiation, softmax algebra, warp-15 producer, dP/dS computation, tensor
MMA order, and frontier kernel were unchanged. The dPsum stage is acknowledged
only after the loaded value is consumed by dP.

Perturbing this path exposed an existing dense/frontier overlap race rather
than a numerical defect in the direct loader. Intermittent failures corrupted
complete dK chunks belonging to one 2-CTA cluster, most often in the last
head; dV remained exact and dQ stayed within its normal atomic drift. Targeted
runs established the following:

| Configuration | Repeated result |
| --- | --- |
| frontier only | stable |
| dense only with concurrent frontier | intermittent whole-chunk dK corruption |
| dense only with frontier serialized | stable |
| dense output zero-prefilled | failed chunks were nonzero, ruling out omitted stores |

The missing edge was between the four reducer warps' in-place Q transpose and
the compute warp that publishes `dkdv_operands_ready`. `q_source_loaded`
proved only that every reducer had loaded the original Q before any reducer
overwrote the shared tile; it did not prove that all four transposed stores
were visible before dK MMA consumed Q. Faster direct-statistics execution and
frontier contention changed the timing enough to expose this latent hazard.

The fix adds a four-arrival `q_transpose_ready` semaphore to the split-LSE
family. Each reducer executes an async-shared fence after its Q stores and
arrives; compute warp 4 waits for all arrivals before the existing cluster
multicast of `dkdv_operands_ready`. No dense/frontier host serialization is
added. After the fix, 800 concurrent dense-only calls with zero-prefilled
outputs and 800 normal merged calls produced no dK report. A fresh synchronized

### Split dV/dK Readiness Pipeline

warp still waited for the complete dS and normal-dO preparation before issuing
any output MMA. The dV MMA needs only the already-published shared P tile and
normal-layout dO; dK alone needs the later dS/Q handoff. A private
B1/S16384/H8 specialization therefore moves the existing compute-owned dO

single `dkdv_done` edge. This is distinct from the rejected reducer early-dV
probe: it adds no P TMEM round trip, reducer role, or shared allocation, and it
reuses the established compute dO gather and shared P tile.

### Dead-P dQ-A Handoff After dV

Splitting dV readiness creates a new storage lifetime that the earlier fused
probes did not have: after the separately committed dV MMA completes, shared P
is dead even though dK remains in flight. A private B1/S16384/H8 specialization
reinterprets that 32 KiB P slot as the dQ-A tile. Compute warps form dS, use a
256-thread named barrier to finish all P reads, wait for the real dV completion
edge, and assemble local/peer dQ-A halves into the recycled P storage while dK
is still executing. The MMA warp then issues dQ immediately after dK on the
same tensor pipe, so the dQ completion edge also covers prior dK work. This is
not the rejected dS-in-Q/dO overlap: Q, dO, and dS storage are never
overwritten, and P is recycled only after a true dV completion.

### Role-Kernel Q-Transpose Contract

The Q-to-dK race fix was previously conditional on `PipelineLsePrefetch`,
although every role-kernel specialization performs the same in-place Q
transpose. The first production generalization made the four-reducer
`q_transpose_ready` edge unconditional. It was correct, but two same-seed
S16384/H16 passes measured `6.947840/6.940160 ms`, about 0.5-0.6% above the
historical paired control (`6.905600/6.904064 ms`).

The final contract folds those four reducer arrivals into the existing eight
compute-warp `dkdv_local_ready` barrier. Its expected count is now 12; reducer
warps arrive only after the async-shared fence following all transposed Q
stores, and compute warp 4 publishes `dkdv_operands_ready` after the single
combined wait. Thus every role specialization has the dependency without a
second semaphore or polling loop.

completion and kept it in storage aliased with the Q/dO handoff. A new exact
B1/S16384/H16 private specialization splits dV readiness from paired-owner
output-drain reuse, commits dV completion independently, and stages dQ-A in
the dead P tile while dK is still running. Q and dO are not overwritten early;
the existing Q-transpose contract and causal frontier are unchanged.

#### CuTe 2-CTA K-Operand Check

Source inspection also falsified a proposed score-K reuse hypothesis. In the
SM100 2-CTA path CuTe allocates separate `sK` and `sKt` shared tensors and a
separate `pipeline_Kt`: `sK` feeds score MMA while `sKt` feeds dQ MMA. Only
the non-2-CTA path aliases the transposed view onto `sK`. TK similarly loads
score K into its `128x192` score layout and dQ K into the distributed
`256x96` layout. The remaining approximately 2.02x H16 gap cannot be closed
by assuming CuTe performs one physical K load, and the already rejected raw
shared-layout reinterpretation and direct dQ-K TMA probes should not be
repeated.

#### CuTe Q/dO Load Contract and Distributed Shortcut (Rejected)

Generated CuTe DSL IR/PTX/cubin for the SM100 BF16 backward kernel confirms
that its D192 2-CTA mainloop performs distinct Q, transposed-Q, dO, and
transposed-dO loads. In particular, the dK B descriptor uses instruction
descriptor `0x10210490`, descriptor high bits `0x40004040`, a 16-byte leading
dimension, a 1024-byte stride, and 128-byte swizzle; consecutive K chunks
advance by 2048 bytes. The dV B descriptor separately uses `0x10310490` and
high bits `0x80004020`. CuTe therefore does not reinterpret the score-Q or dP
dO bytes as the dK/dV operands.

This falsified the private distributed-Q/dO shortcut that skipped peer
exchange without constructing the required transposed layouts. Its partial
binding and kernel edits were removed completely before the next build. The
production Q-transpose-to-dK completion edge remains enabled in every retained
role-kernel route that transposes Q, including split-LSE, direct-statistics,
N192, paired direct-Q/dO, and the BF16-output route below.

#### H16 Critical Path And Distributed Statistics Cache (Rejected)

A fresh bounded S16384/H16 comparison of pushed `471c49a` confirms that the
remaining graph gap is dense-main work, not the frontier tail. Nsys measured
TK preprocess/dense/frontier/merge at
`37.568/4919.200/771.936/97.696 us`. The frontier starts at `4301.888 us`
while dense ends at `5007.904 us`, so it overlaps about `706 us` and extends
the critical path by only about `66 us`. CuTe preprocess/main/postprocess is
`51.264/2935.456/69.856 us`; TK dense alone is therefore `1.676x` CuTe main.

The launch structure remains materially different. TK launches `1024` CTAs
in `512` two-CTA clusters (`6.74` waves/SM), while CuTe launches `2048` CTAs
in `1024` two-CTA clusters (`13.47` waves/SM). Both use 512 threads and 128
registers/thread. TK uses `231292 B` shared versus CuTe `224256 B`. The prior
H16 single-owner test already showed that doubling TK's grid without reducing
its per-owner serial work regresses by about 7.9%, so the grid difference is
diagnostic rather than an optimization by itself.

Fresh SourceCounters on the score-fanin dense kernel identify the current
handoffs. The loader's `dq_done` wait collected `3522` samples (`3506`
long-scoreboard); `dq_reduce_done` collected `1073` (`1051`
long-scoreboard). The MMA path collected `1475` samples at
`dp_operands_ready`, `859` at `dv_operands_ready`, and `1342` at
`dkdv_done`. Direct statistics loads generated `10,485,760` global sectors,
of which `5,242,880` were excessive; their CUDA-header source row collected

#### Packed-P And No-Extra-SMEM Adjacent Pipeline (Rejected)

The exact packed-P prerequisite was resolved before testing adjacent-tile
overlap. TK's generic packed TMEM reload is not the inverse of its plain BF16
`STTM`: an isolated two-CTA round trip produced `32498/32768` mismatches. The
MMA-compatible inverse keeps the plain store and uses explicit
`LDTM.16x128b.x8` loads at physical row
`32*(warp%4)+16*(warp/4)` and packed-column stride `j*8`. This was bit-exact
and deterministic. The corresponding H16 production specialization compiled
at REG 128, STACK/LOCAL 0, SHARED `231308 B`, with true `UTCHMMA.2CTA` and no
spills. It passed the established first-call and 50-call correctness gates,
but packed P alone lost reproducibly by `0.125%` and `0.151%` in two rotated
201-sample processes (`5.197152/5.190656 ms` and
`5.191488/5.183648 ms`, probe/parent).

A private B1/S16384/H16 prologue/main/tail probe then tested the proposed
no-extra-SMEM schedule: TMA Q(next) into the freed 32-KiB `main.p`, copy it to
`main.q` after dK(cur), and reuse `main.p` for dQ(cur). An exact-offset `/tmp`
two-CTA microprobe reproduced production offsets (`main.q=98304`,
`main.p=139264`) and proved both the Q TMA source and logical shared copy
bit-exact across five calls. Production testing nevertheless exposed three
separate lifetime failures:

* Loading dO(next) into `main.dout` after the dV commit made all dQ/dK/dV
  outputs non-finite. Deferring dO until after dQ removed the non-finites, so
  the dV commit is not a sufficient publication point for reusing that shared
  operand.
* The first storage-only version used the owner-adjusted phase for a barrier
  that receives an even number of arrivals per owner pass. That let pass two
  reuse `main.q` before dK completion; switching it to `iteration & 1`
  restored dK/dV to the fallback envelope.
* Publishing `qdo_ready(next)` before `dq_reduce_done(cur)` let score(next)
  overwrite the score/P TMEM region while reducers still drained dQ(cur).
  dQ tiles 0/1 and the no-next tail were exact, while tiles 2:126 accumulated
  progressively larger errors. Moving publication after the dQ drain restored
  first-call dQ parity (maximum difference from the parent `2.24e-8`).

The fully corrected storage-only form compiled at REG 128, STACK/LOCAL 0,
SHARED `231340 B` with no spills. Its first call had dQ/dK/dV relative-L2
`0.00313919/0.00372004/0.00215796` and maxima
`0.00827026/0.015625/0.03125`. It still failed the 50-call gate: maximum
dQ/dK/dV drift was `0.04432/0.04611/0.03540`, with up to `33,142,904`
varying dQ elements. The packed-P flag, adjacent barriers, private binding,
and production route were therefore rejected rather than timed. The evidence
rules out another alias-based no-extra-SMEM attempt; a future adjacent-tile
pipeline needs a genuinely disjoint Q/dO/V stage and must retain the
`dq_reduce_done` publication contract.

#### Disjoint V/P/dS Storage Contract (Correct, Rejected)

CuTe's 2-CTA shared layout keeps `sV`, `sdO`, and `sdS` independent, whereas
the TK role kernel restages persistent V into `storage.ds` before every dP
and then overwrites that allocation with dS. A private exact B1/S16384/H16
probe tested a no-growth storage contract before changing publication order:
packed P remained in TMEM columns `320:383`, dP used `384:511`, the freed
32-KiB `main.p` held V, and `storage.ds` was reused for dQ only after a true
dK-completion barrier. The dQ reducer's 32-KiB ring then reused `storage.ds`
only after `dq_done`; the existing loader-side `dq_reduce_done` wait protected
the following dS publication.

Two first-call failures exposed useful lifetime distinctions. The retained
`dkdv_done` barrier is published after dV but before dK because it protects
dead-P reuse; using it to overwrite `storage.ds` made dK/dQ non-finite. A
separate tcgen dK completion fixed that edge. The next version left the dQ
reducer ring in `main.p`, which overwrote persistent V and again made dK/dQ
non-finite while dV stayed exact. Moving that post-`dq_done` ring to the now
dead dS allocation fixed the second edge. Neither failure was timed.

The final specialization compiled to 84 true `UTCHMMA.2CTA` sites with REG
128, STACK/LOCAL 0, SHARED `231308 B`, and no spills. One call matched the
score-fanin parent exactly for dK/dV and within `2.24e-8` maximum for dQ. A
50-call gate measured dQ/dK/dV relative-L2
`0.0031446191/0.0037249147/0.0021510995` and maxima
`0.0092972517/0.015625/0.015625`; dK/dV were bit-exact and maximum dQ drift
was `5.9604645e-08`.

The independent stage nevertheless regressed reproducibly before any
adjacent-score publication was attempted:

| Seed | CuTe ms | score-fanin parent ms | disjoint-V ms | probe / parent |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20277391 | `3.135520` | `5.185792` | `5.576704` | `1.075381` |
| 20277392 | `3.124928` | `5.182624` | `5.572864` | `1.075298` |

The packed-P reload plus explicit dK publication and dS/dQ reducer reuse
cost about 7.5%, so this is not a viable base for another alias-based

#### Looped dQ Issue Body (Correct, Rejected)

The CuTe dQ PTX has eight static MMA sites inside a two-iteration descriptor
loop, so it executes the same sixteen dQ MMAs per dense tile as TK. An exact
B1/S16384/H16 private probe compressed TK's sixteen static sites to one
eight-MMA inline-PTX body with a non-unrolled two-phase loop. The linked
specialization used REG 128, STACK/LOCAL 0, SHARED `231292 B`, no `LDL`/`STL`,
and 76 total `UTCHMMA.2CTA` sites instead of the parent's 84. Its dQ window had
one static `ELECT`, eight MMAs, and a back edge that executed the body twice.

The first encoding reversed the two descriptor strides and was rejected at
the one-call gate: dQ relative-L2 was `1.04374`. Parent SASS proved that the
first `AtB` descriptor advances by `0x80` and the second by `0x40`; correcting
those strides restored dQ parity. The corrected 50-call gate had dQ/dK/dV
relative-L2 `0.00313919/0.00372004/0.00215796`, dK/dV were bit-exact, and the
maximum dQ drift was `2.23517e-8`.

The code-size reduction was reproducibly slower than the retained loader

| Score | MMA warp issues 12 group-2 MMAs; compute warps wait, load score from TMEM, apply scaled `exp2`, and produce P | same 12 MMAs and TMEM score drain; score consumption is synchronized through TK named barriers |
| P publication | packed P remains in TMEM rows `320:447` | P is published through shared-memory `STSM` paths |
| dP/dS | eight dP MMAs write TMEM rows `384:511`; compute warps load dP, form dS, store dS to TMEM, and publish the peer half in shared memory | eight dP MMAs; compute warps form dS and publish the full shared dS tile with `STSM` |
| Peer dS handoff | one contiguous 16 KiB `cp.async.bulk.shared::cluster...mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes` per CTA | retained route used eight contiguous 2 KiB bulk copies per CTA from the already-complete full dS tile |
| dK/dV | eight dK plus eight dV group-2 MMAs consume the on-chip operands | eight dV then eight dK group-2 MMAs; the Q-to-dK transpose is TK-specific |
| dQ | 16 dynamic dQ MMAs accumulate into the upper TMEM region; four reducer warps drain fixed fragments to registers/shared and issue TMA reduce-add | 16 dQ MMAs; four reducer warps use the corrected superlane drain, shared staging, and TMA reduce-add |
| Completion | staged pipeline producer/consumer barriers cover all publications; the main kernel also owns the causal frontier | explicit Q/dO, score, dP, dS exchange, dK/dV, dQ, and output handoffs; causal frontier remains a separate kernel |

The generated CuTe PTX around the peer exchange moves literal `16384` into
the transaction byte count, performs `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx`, maps the
peer shared address with `mapa.shared::cluster`, and emits one
`cp.async.bulk.shared::cluster.shared::cta.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes`.
TK's retained SASS instead executes eight `UBLKCP.S.S` instructions per CTA.
This is a publication-granularity difference, not a difference in tensor
math.

SourceCounters normalized by logical tile make that distinction explicit:

| Dynamic instruction family | CuTe / tile | TK / tile | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `UTCHMMA.2CTA` | `52` | `52` | tensor work is equal |
| `LDTM` | `~89.25` | `~89.25` | TMEM load count is effectively equal |
| `MUFU` | `1024` | `1024` | score exponent work is equal |
| `F2FP` | `~1044` | `~1044` | conversion work is equal |
| `UBLKCP.S.S` | `2` | `16` | one CuTe peer-dS copy/CTA versus eight TK copies/CTA |
| `STSM` | n/a | `515` | TK shared transpose/publication path |
| `STTM` | `64` | n/a | CuTe keeps P/dS publications in TMEM |
| scalar `FMUL` | negligible | `~768` | known TK scaling path; prior packed-FMA replacements regressed |
| `R2UR` | `~365` | `~1386` | TK address/control overhead |
| `VIADD` | `~131` | `~988` | TK address/control overhead |
| `LOP3` | `~421` | `~1475` | TK address/control overhead |
| `IMAD` | `~760` | `~2346` | TK address/control overhead |
| `WARPSYNC` | `~0.8` | `~146` | TK transpose/control overhead |

The retained TK kernel executes `1,320,551,264` warp instructions versus
CuTe's `1,022,246,200` for the capture. CuTe actually executes more pipeline
`SYNCS` per tile (`~2918` versus `~1826`), so total synchronization count is
not a useful optimization target. TK's hottest sampled PCs remain the eight
score `LDTM` sites (`97,160` samples, `97,040` barrier stalls) and reducer
`S2R` (`35,381` samples, `35,248` barrier stalls); the corresponding
score-fanout and dQ issue/fanout experiments are already rejected. The new,
falsifiable target was therefore narrower: replace only the eight already
legal 2 KiB peer-dS transactions with one 16 KiB transaction per CTA while
preserving the existing full-dS completion barrier and every consumer.

#### dQ-before-dK Tensor/Reducer Overlap (Incorrect, Rejected)

The next exact H16 child tested whether the reducer's dominant dQ-completion

and committed dQ immediately after the existing dV completion and operand
handoff, then queued dK. The intended SASS order was present: score, dP, dV,
sixteen dQ MMAs plus completion, then the N192 dK first/accumulate branches.
Candidate and parent were both REG 128, STACK/LOCAL 0 and SHARED `231292 B`,
with no spills and 68 total `UTCHMMA.2CTA` sites.

The first synchronized call rejected the overlap. dQ and dV retained their
CuTe-relative errors (`0.00313919` and `0.00215796`), but dK relative-L2 rose
to `0.62020` and dK changed between route invocations. Every 32-feature dK
band was wrong (`0.56509-0.67318` relative-L2), ruling out a tail mapping
error. The failure was initially attributed to overlapping dQ drain and the
live N192 dK accumulator, but a subsequent lifetime audit found a narrower
overwrite. The reducer's dQ TMEM columns are disjoint from dK, and its shared
drain stage aliases the already-dead `main.p`. However, this exact route uses
`dq_done` as permission to TMA the next Q/dO directly over `main.q` and
`main.dout`. Moving `dq_done` ahead of dK therefore overwrote
`main.q.normal_wide` while current N192 dK still consumed it. This exactly
accounts for the global, nondeterministic dK corruption. A valid follow-up must
protect that Q-to-dK operand lifetime while still allowing the dQ reducer to
overlap dK; simply
waiting for dQ drain before dK would restore the original serialization. The
invalid route was not stress-tested or timed, and all private source and
harness edits were removed.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Work ownership | Grid `(128,16,1)`: 64 two-CTA clusters/head, one K owner/cluster, with the causal frontier integrated | Grid `(64,16,1)`: 32 clusters/head, two mirrored owner passes/cluster; frontier is a separate kernel |

| K publication | `sK` is the score operand and a separately TMA-published `sKt` is the dQ operand | Score K is already TMA-published by the exact route; the retained dQ K path separately uses twelve `LDG.E.128` and twelve `STS.128` sites |
| dO publication | For D192, `sdOt` is a recast view of `sdO`; one TMA stage supplies dP and dV | The dP layout is loaded first and eight compute warps form the dV layout through shared matrix load/store and named-barrier handoffs |
| Score/P | 12 `UTCHMMA.2CTA`; compute loads S from TMEM, applies packed scale/subtract plus `MUFU.EX2`, and writes packed P to overlapping TMEM with `STTM` | Same 12 MMAs, score TMEM drain, exponent and conversion counts; P is instead published through shared `STSM` for dV |
| dP/dS | Eight dP MMAs; compute drains dP, forms dS, writes dS to overlapping TMEM, and retains only the exchange half for shared publication | Eight dP MMAs; compute forms dS, publishes a full shared tile for dK/dQ, and also writes the TMEM dS view used by retained paths |
| Peer dS | One 16 KiB cluster bulk copy/CTA with expected-byte mbarrier accounting | Retained one 16 KiB cluster bulk copy/CTA after the full-dS completion contract |
| dK/dV | Eight dK then eight dV MMAs consume TMEM P/dS and TMA shared operands | Eight dV then eight dK MMAs consume TK's published layouts; changing issue order alone is already rejected |
| dQ/reduce | Sixteen dynamic dQ MMAs, four reducers use raw `LDTM.x32`, ordinary `STS.128`, and staged TMA reduce-add | Same 16 dynamic MMAs and corrected four-reducer TMEM drain; explicit reducer fanout and completion handoffs remain |

Tensor and nonlinear work are already matched: both execute 52

The first candidate selected from the raw opcode block was rejected at the
static gate before runtime. A proposed distributed score-K load conflicted

correlation showed that the 64 scalar `LDG.E` sites are the four reducer

publication. They are not score-K traffic. The private flag and binding were
removed without running correctness or timing; all three backward sources
again byte-match `b1c4e22`.

This correction narrows the remaining data-movement gap further. Score K and
dQ K already use their intended independent publications, and previous
TMA/persistent-V experiments show that changing V ownership or lifetime is
not a new hypothesis. Any next child must preserve reducer-owned V and change
only a demonstrably expensive publication or transpose primitive, or target a
different CuTe/TK phase difference with a separately falsifiable dependency

from each aligned 16-byte half-row, and the four register-tile values map to
column halves `0:8` and `8:16`. The proof covered all 32 lanes, two row tiles,

body, but failed the mandatory no-spill gate. Holding four aligned load

CuTe uses a `(128,128)` logical tile, 512 threads, two-CTA clusters, REG 128,

a separate frontier grid handles the diagonal. The short route instead has a
416-thread REG-128/STACK-24/SHARED-216212 dQ grid and a 288-thread
REG-168/STACK-64/SHARED-199748 clustered dK/dV grid.

H16 is not bandwidth-volume or tensor-work bound: TK reads only 11.1% and
writes 12.7% more DRAM bytes per tile, has less L2 traffic, and issues the
same 26 tensor MMAs, yet its dense main is 58.4% slower. The scalable
difference is shared-layout construction and address/control work: about
2.97x IMAD, 3.21x LOP3, 6.01x VIADD and 178x WARPSYNC, with a 24-point L1-hit
deficit. H8 additionally executes four dK MMAs per owner iteration because it
retains split N128+N64 dK. This is not untested: paired unified-N192 H8 was
correct but reproducibly regressed by `0.29-0.33%`. H16 already uses the
retained unified-N192 route.

The exact H16 sampled PCs assign the largest unmatched address block,
relative `0x2320..0x2b50`, to the already-rejected dQ drain/TMA-reduce path.
The next compute-side block, `0xa440..0xa8d0`, performs the shared P reload,
dO publication, and dP TMEM drain. Its generic P reload contributes repeated
LDSM address construction and a per-warp `WARPSYNC`; a byte-identical custom
P reload is the next bounded hypothesis. It changes neither P publication,
packed/TMEM P, dQ, waits, V ownership, nor default dispatch.

##### Exact-H16 direct shared-P reload: rejected at the static gate

The bounded child replaced only the compute warp's
`warp::load(rt_bf<16,128>, st_bf<16,128>)` P reload. The helper computed the
first swizzled address once, used XOR offsets `0x20 * j` for the four 16-column
tiles in a 64-column swizzle sector, and added `0x4000` bytes for the second
sector. This is byte-identical for the concrete layout: BF16 elements, 128
underlying rows, 128-byte swizzle, and a 128-byte-aligned shared base. An
exhaustive host check over eight possible base residues, all 128 rows, 32
lanes, and eight register-tile columns compared 262144 address pairs with zero
mismatches. The second sector is `128 rows * 64 columns * 2 bytes = 0x4000`,
which also preserves the address modulo the 1024-byte swizzle repeat.

The child was exposed only through an exact B1/S16384/H16 private binding. The

##### Exact-H16 integrated causal frontier: retained private route

The separate frontier has disjoint ownership that can be folded into the
current clustered role kernel without a new accumulation race. At S16384,
there are 128 Q/KV blocks and 64 owner indices. Owner `o` exclusively stores
K/V blocks `2o` and `2o+1`, one per CTA rank. The retained dense loop begins
at Q block `2o+1` and suppresses CTA rank 1 there, so it omits exactly two
tiles per owner: `(Q,K)=(2o,2o)` and `(2o+1,2o+1)`. The private child begins
at Q block `2o` and applies these ownership rules:

| Q block | CTA rank 0 / K block `2o` | CTA rank 1 / K block `2o+1` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2o` | triangular diagonal | zero |
| `2o+1` | full | triangular diagonal |
| later | full | full |

Each diagonal contribution therefore enters the owning CTA's existing FP32
TMEM dK/dV accumulator before its sole BF16 global store. dQ continues through
the existing reduce-add handoff and has no new exclusive-store requirement.
This is materially different from the old generic integrated-frontier kernel,
which compiled at REG 168 with `600/680 B` spills and regressed. The child
reuses the current REG-128 role schedule, adds one masked iteration per owner,
and changes only an exact B1/S16384/H16 private binding. Default dispatch and
all other shape routes remain unchanged.

##### Exact-H16 launch-domain assumptions: rejected on repeated correctness

The retained exact S16384/H16 route already folds its causal diagonal into
the clustered main. Cluster owner `o`, rank `r` is the sole dK/dV writer for
K/V tile `2*o+r`; q tile `2*o+r` is its unique diagonal, the earlier
cross-rank tile is masked, and dQ uses reduce-add across these disjoint K
owners. There is consequently no separate frontier scratch/add launch to
remove at this shape. Folding another diagonal into the main would duplicate
dK/dV or dQ ownership, so that path was closed statically.

A distinct exact-shape private child told ptxas the host-proven launch ranges
`head_idx < 16`, `owner_pair_idx < 64`, and `cta_rank < 2` through
`__builtin_assume`, without changing operands, barriers, ownership, or the
retained elected score-K path. The explicit GPU-1 build passed the initial
resource/SASS gate:

##### Cheaper dP-TMEM release refinements: rejected by the 2000-call gate

Two bounded exact-H16 refinements attempted to remove the full compute-warp
`bar.sync 9,256` without reopening the known score/dP TMEM generation race.
Both kept the tensor producer's `score_consumed` phase wait and were compared
only against the correct full-release parent.

The first child piggybacked release on the existing dK/dV fan-in barrier 7:
all compute warps reached the barrier after their dP load, reducer warps also
arrived, and compute warp 4 published the cluster release after
`bar.sync 7,384`. It remained REG 128, STACK/LOCAL 0, spill-free, and grew
from `5160` to `5168` decoded instructions. One-call and 50-call checks
passed, but the critical seed `20260768` failed at call 133: maximum dQ drift
was `0.03828933`, dK drift was `0.0439453125`, and dV remained exact. The
fan-in barrier is therefore not a valid dP-consumer generation boundary.

The second child had each of the eight compute warps per CTA publish directly
after its own `tensor_load_wait()`, with the cluster semaphore expecting 16
arrivals. Static resources remained REG 128, STACK/LOCAL 0, SHARED
`231276 B`, with no spills and 52 `UTCHMMA.2CTA`. It removed the barrier-9
sync but added eight address/control instructions (`5168` total); `WARPSYNC`
and producer try-wait counts were unchanged. One-call seed `20260930` was
numerically identical to the correct parent apart from `2.98023e-08` dQ, and
the 50-call seed `20260931` kept dK/dV exact with maximum dQ drift
`2.98023e-08`. The mandatory 2000-call seed nevertheless failed at call 539:
maximum dQ drift was `0.00969770`, dK drift was `0.01049805`, and dV stayed
exact. Per-warp arrival does not provide the collective ordering needed
between all TMEM loads and producer reuse.

Neither incorrect child was timed. Both were removed completely. The three
backward source files again byte-match pushed `6ab73d7`, and the explicit
GPU-1 safe rebuild completed successfully. A fresh 50-call control (seed
`20260934`) kept all outputs finite, dK/dV repeat-exact, and dQ drift at
`2.98023e-08`; CuTe-relative dQ/dK/dV relative-L2 was
`0.00328106/0.00354251/0.00007909`, with maxima
`0.0241513/0.015625/0.00390625`.

The retained full release remains the correctness baseline. Its prior
2000-call proof had exact dK/dV and only `2.98023e-08` dQ drift, and its two
fully synchronized timing gates measured `4790.629` and `4792.132 us`, or

release optimization must reproduce CuTe's collective consumer-release
ordering rather than infer completion from an unrelated fan-in or independent

##### Split-collective dP-TMEM release: retained exact-H16 opt-in

CuTe's BF16 compute path establishes the relevant contract explicitly:
each compute warp completes and fences its dP TMEM load, the compute group
rendezvouses, and only an elected warp releases the pipeline stage. A private
exact `B=1,S=16384,H=16` child preserved that collective edge while splitting
the eight compute warps into two independent four-warp groups. Warps 4--7 use
named barrier 9 with 128 participants, warps 8--11 use barrier 10 with 128
participants, and one leader from each subgroup and CTA publishes to the
rank-0 cluster semaphore (expected count 4). The tensor warp retains the same
post-dQ phase wait before score/dP TMEM reuse.

dynamic counters, not conclusions inferred from static SASS counts.

Phase mapping against `flash_bwd_sm100.py` confirms that both main loops
issue the same score, dP, dK, dV, and dQ tensor work. CuTe keeps P/dS in
TMEM and uses recast Q/dO layouts; TK republishes more operands through
shared memory and carries more scalar address/control state. Existing
experiments already rejected the direct TK analogues of retained-P/dS,
recast Q/dO, V publication, and dQ-drain changes, so those families remain
closed. Ranked remaining hypotheses from this capture are:

1. Remove scalar address/control work inside the live owner loop, especially
   work repeated per score tile, without changing operand layouts.
2. Reduce a correctness-proven collective synchronization site only when the
   2000-call generation test proves the replacement contract.
3. Revisit ownership granularity only with a dataflow that reduces shared
   publication; CTA count alone is not causal because CuTe uses more CTAs.

Two cheaper release refinements were rejected statically before runtime.
A register-selected subgroup barrier decoded to `5192` instructions versus
the split parent's `5184` with unchanged resources and wait sites. Caching
the reducer's `score_done` wait address also decoded to the same `5184`
instructions and retained all four compiler-generated address constructions.
Both probes were removed without runtime testing.

and CTA rank owns the diagonal offset. Therefore the two score conditions are
equivalently `iteration == cta_rank` for diagonal masking and
`iteration < cta_rank` for the rank-1 invalid prefix. A private terminal
template flag applies those iteration-relative predicates only to exact

index comparisons.

The correctness-proven split release still left four compute warps in each

tensor producer waits for all eight cluster arrivals (four per CTA) before
reusing the score/dP generation. This preserves a collective completion edge
for every consumer and is not the rejected per-warp-arrival or barrier-7
piggyback protocol.

##### Exact-H16 dynamic register allocation parity

The matched CuTe/TK SASS comparison resolves the open `USETMAXREG` question.
CuTe does use role-specific dynamic register reallocation, but the retained
TK role kernel already implements the same budget and role count. CuTe assigns
warps 0--3 to reduction, 4--11 to compute, 12 to MMA, 13 to load, 14 to relay,
and 15 to empty. Its source budget is `136 + 2*136 + 104 = 512` registers per
warp group, with the load/MMA/relay roles at 104 and the empty role at 24.

| Role | Warps | CuTe exact SASS site | TK quarter-route exact SASS site | Dynamic registers |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| reduce | `0--3` | `0xb420 TRY_ALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x88` | `0x10c0 TRY_ALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x88` | `136` |
| compute | `4--11` | `0x7640 TRY_ALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x88` | `0x74e0 TRY_ALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x88` | `136` |
| MMA | `12` | `0x37b0 DEALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x68` | `0xcfe0 DEALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x68` | `104` |
| load | `13` | `0x1820 DEALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x68` | `0xfe00 DEALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x68` | `104` |
| relay | `14` | `0x1300 DEALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x68` | `0x128c0 DEALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x68` | `104` |
| empty | `15` | `0x12d0 DEALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x18` | `0xfdc0 DEALLOC.CTAPOOL 0x18` | `24` |

Both exact kernels report a static 128-register envelope, while the dynamic
pool reallocates those registers between roles. A new `setmaxnreg` child is
therefore inapplicable: it would duplicate the current topology rather than
address the wall-time gap, and the retained configuration is already
occupancy-safe at one 512-thread cluster CTA pair per SM partition.

The phase-normalized SourceCounters comparison instead leaves a compute-side
address/control gap. Per matched exact-H16 capture, TK executes `721.54M`
compute-role instructions versus CuTe's `569.92M`, while both execute
`68.16M MUFU.EX2` operations and essentially the same BF16 packing work.
TK has `69.76M IMAD.U32`, `36.75M PRMT`, `61.28M LOP3`, and `37.20M VIADD`
in that phase versus CuTe's `25.82M`, approximately zero, `26.97M`, and
`8.73M`, respectively. The next probes must reduce this data-layout/address
work without disturbing the already-matched register-role contract.

##### Native packed-P mapping proof and disjoint-TMEM child: correct, slower

The previous deterministic packed-P relative error near `0.108` was isolated
with `/tmp/tk_bf16_tmem_p_roundtrip_probe.{cu,py}` before another production
edit. For physical compute warp `w = physical_warp - 4`, score-TMEM `x32`
register `r` maps to logical

```text
row = 128 * cta_rank + 32 * (w % 4) + lane
col = 32 * (w < 4) + 64 * stage + r
```

The matching packed-BF16 P publication uses physical row
`32 * (w % 4)` and packed column `16 * (w < 4) + 32 * stage`; packed word
`i` contains score registers `2*i` and `2*i+1`. CuTe's apparent `+16` in
the retained-P PTX is therefore a packed TMEM-column offset, not a physical
row offset. The exact inverse uses physical rows `0,32,64,96` for the first
four group warps and `16,48,80,112` for the second four.

On GPU 1 the raw map covered all `32768` logical P elements exactly once:
minimum `0`, maximum `32767`, `32768` unique values, and zero permutation
mismatches. Native score-x32 to packed-P roundtrip had relative-L2 `0`, max
absolute error `0`, and zero mismatches globally and in every 16-row block;
five repeats were bit-exact. TK's normal `group<8>::store_async` followed by
the explicit `16x128b.x8` inverse was also element-exact. In contrast, the
generic grouped reload had `32498/32768` mismatches. This proves the old
error was the reload permutation, not score arithmetic or BF16 conversion.

The exact-H16 private child reused the retained parent's stack-free FP32
score/P transform and normal STTM publication. It placed packed P in disjoint
TMEM columns `448:512`, let score and dP reuse `320:448` in successive
generations, and reloaded P through the proven explicit x8 inverse. It kept
the proven split dP-consumer release and all other role ownership unchanged.
Earlier raw-fragment implementations were statically rejected without
runtime: retaining 64 FP32 values produced STACK `256`; progressively
chunking the drain reduced spill traffic from `116/124` to `100/100` and then
`20/20` bytes but did not meet the zero-spill gate.

The final exact child passed the static gate at REG `128`, STACK/LOCAL/spills
`0`, SHARED `231276 B`, matching the parent resources. Its exact SASS removed
12 static `STSM` and four `LDSM` sites, while adding two `STTM.16`, two
`LDTM.16`, and two proxy-barrier sites. Decoded instructions increased
`5176 -> 5240`. The child contains 60 static `UTCHMMA.2CTA` sites versus 52
in the parent because the TMEM-P dV path emits alternate eight-site first-
accumulation and accumulate branches; only one branch executes, so dynamic
MMA intent remains 52 per owner iteration. Neither exact symbol contains
`LDL` or `STL`.

All correctness gates passed. One-call seed `20260977` gave parent/child
CuTe-relative dQ/dK/dV relative-L2
`0.00327309/0.00355500/0.00008102`; child dK/dV were bit-exact to parent and
dQ differed by at most `2.23517e-08`. The 50-call seed `20260978` kept every

##### Early dQ-A publication over fused TMEM dK/dV: retained exact-H16 win

The fused TMEM P+dS route changes the lifetime that had made earlier dQ-A
publication-overlap probes illegal. After `qdo_exchange_done`, P is consumed
from TMEM `448:512`, dS is consumed from TMEM `320:448`, dV reads
`main.dout`, and dK reads `main.q`; none of those tensor phases reads
`main.p`. The loader also waits `dq_done` before reusing `main` for the next
Q/dO pair. It is therefore race-free for the eight compute warps to publish
the current local dS half directly into `main.p`, stage the peer half in the
already-consumed `qdo_phase`, and launch the existing 16 KiB peer bulk copy
immediately after dS formation. The tensor warp still executes the unchanged
dV -> dK -> dQ order, but the dQ-A shared stores, proxy fence, CTA barrier,
and peer copy can now overlap dV/dK instead of following `dkdv_done`.

##### Wide packed-P TMEM load: mapping-exact, static rejection

The retained packed-P path was re-derived and tested independently before a
production edit. For compute warp `w`, the native score `LDTM.x32` maps lane
`l` to physical row `128*cta_rank + 32*(w%4) + l`; its columns are
`32*(w<4) + 64*stage + register`. Two adjacent FP32 score registers are
converted to one BF16x2 word. The retained-P `STTM.x16` maps that word to
physical row `32*(w%4) + l` and column
`16*(w<4) + 32*stage + word`. Therefore the inverse compute fragment starts
at physical row `32*(w%4) + 16*(w/4)`, and output register
`4*tile + element` maps directly to `rt_bf<16,128>::tiles[0][tile].data[element]`.

An isolated GPU-1 diagnostic added one
`tcgen05.ld.sync.aligned.16x128b.x16.b32` alongside the current two
`16x128b.x8` loads and stored both through the same `warp::store` consumer:

```bash

  -f /tmp/Makefile.tk_bf16_tmem_p_roundtrip_probe
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 timeout 120s \
  python /tmp/tk_bf16_tmem_p_roundtrip_probe.py
```

Both loaders matched every one of the `32768` logical P elements, all sixteen
16-row blocks, and five repeats exactly: relative-L2 `0`, max error `0`, zero
mismatches. The generated probe SASS contained the intended single
`LDTM.16dp128bit.x16`. This resolves the former deterministic packed-P error:
it came from TK's generic grouped reload permutation, not from native FP32 P
or the retained-P `STTM` layout.

all publication, ownership, split dP-consumer release, and owner-boundary

##### Single score/dK Q publication: standalone mapping rejection

The exact CuTe D192 layouts were extracted from a fresh B1/S16384/H16
specialization before considering another production recast. Its score-Q
layout is K-major SW128 with outer layout
`((64,16),1,(4,3),1):((64,1),0,(16,4096),0)` and its dK-Q view is MN-major
SW64 with outer layout
`(((32,3),16),1,8,1):(((1,4096),32),0,512,0)`. Both have `cosize=12288`
BF16 elements. These are exactly TK's local `st_bf<64,192>` and
`st_bf<128,96>` byte formulas, so the prior failure was not an arbitrary
swizzle-width mismatch.

The missing contract is the CTA-local global-tensor partition. Score rank
`r` owns 64 Q rows and all 192 feature columns. dK rank `r` needs all 128 Q
rows and only feature columns `[96*r,96*(r+1))`. Their local sets contain
12288 elements each but intersect in only 6144 elements; no descriptor over
one rank's unchanged 24 KiB score publication can supply the other 6144.
The CuTe source has the same constraint: it issues `load_Q` at
`flash_bwd_sm100.py:2605` and a distinct `load_Qt` at line 2643, reusing the
same allocation only after the score consumer advances the shared Q
pipeline.

A standalone GPU-1 byte-mapping probe populated the shared allocation once
through each view and then read every element through both interpretations:

| Publication / view | mismatches | rel-L2 | max abs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| score publication -> score view | `0 / 24576` | `0` | `0` |
| score publication -> dK view | `24522 / 24576` | `1.416311` | `5.25` |
| dK publication -> dK view | `0 / 24576` | `0` | `0` |
| dK publication -> score view | `24522 / 24576` | `1.416312` | `5.25` |

The probe itself used REG `32`, STACK/spills `0`, and `24576 B` shared. It
was built and run without modifying production sources:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 timeout 900s make -B \
  -f /tmp/Makefile.tk_bf16_q_dual_view_probe
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 timeout 120s \
  python /tmp/tk_bf16_q_dual_view_probe.py
```

Files are `/tmp/tk_bf16_q_dual_view_probe.{cu,py}` and
`/tmp/Makefile.tk_bf16_q_dual_view_probe`. A valid one-publication design
would require an explicit 12 KiB-per-rank cross-CTA transpose or a second
copy, which is the data movement it was intended to remove. The path is
therefore rejected statically; no backward production source changed and
the retained `6799fca` route remains intact.

##### Exact bitwise BF16 P expansion: retained exact-H16 win

The matched CuTe/TK opcode comparison left one open dynamic conversion cost
in TK's retained-P path. `warp::copy(float_fragment, bf16_fragment)` expands
each packed BF16 word through a generic permutation/address sequence. For a
packed word `w = y_bf16 << 16 | x_bf16`, IEEE BF16 widening is bit-exact as
`x_f32_bits = w << 16` and `y_f32_bits = w & 0xffff0000`. A standalone
GPU-1 fragment probe compared every lane, tile, packed register, and scalar
field against `warp::copy`; it reported zero mismatches. The probe used REG
`48`, STACK/spills `0`, and is in `/tmp/tk_bf16_bit_expand_probe.{cu,py}`.

the retained packed P fragment before `dS = P * dP`. P ownership, TMEM and
shared layouts, dP-consumer release, all barriers, dV/dK/dQ MMA paths, and
public/default dispatch are unchanged. The parent route remains available as
the A/B control.

##### Exact bitwise BF16 P expansion: retained S8192/H8 refinement

The packed-fragment mapping proven by the standalone H16 diagnostic is
independent of sequence length and owner count: each lane-local packed word
`w = y_bf16 << 16 | x_bf16` expands exactly as
`x_f32_bits = w << 16`, `y_f32_bits = w & 0xffff0000`. The H8 route uses the
same exact TMEM P loader and register fragment. Its existing contracts already
satisfy fused TMEM P/dS, runtime accumulation, integrated frontier, and
iteration masking, so the compile-time guard was narrowed only from exact 128

##### Fused direct exp2-to-BF16 P pack: rejected S8192/H8 refinement

The H16 fused pack optimization was tested independently on the retained H8
bit-expansion route. Its causal proof holds: integrated frontier starts each
owner at `q=2*owner`; CTA rank 0 starts on its diagonal, while rank 1's first
iteration precedes `kv=2*owner+1` and is the only guaranteed-empty prefix.
The private child therefore packed each direct EX2 result immediately and
wrote zero only for `iteration < cta_rank`, without changing ownership,
barriers, tensor work, or publication.

induction variables. It changed no ownership, publication, barrier, operand,

##### Cached split-dP release cluster address: rejected

The matched H16 SourceCounters trace attributed two `VIADD`, two `LEA`, and
two `PRMT` operations per owner iteration to construction of the two
cluster-mapped split-dP consumer-release destinations.  A private exact
B1/S16384/H16 child cached the `score_consumed` destination before the owner
loop and reused it for the existing two release publishers.  Barrier counts,
phases, ownership, and all four release arrivals were unchanged.

The explicit artifact
`/tmp/tk_fa4_h16_cached_dp_release_C.cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so`
passed its static gate.  Its retained-parent specialization has all `10304`
encoded instructions byte-identical to the fused-exp2 parent.  Parent and
child are both REG `128`, STACK/LOCAL/spills `0`, SHARED `231276 B`, with 52
MMA sites.  In the child, the mapped-address `VIADD + LEA + PRMT` moves from
the repeated hot window near SASS `0xbab0--0xbc20` to the pre-loop window
`0x76e0--0x7720`; the hot release at `0xbe40` consumes the cached register
directly.

Correctness passed: seed `20261158` was finite and child versus parent was
exact for dK/dV with dQ max-abs `1.86265e-08`; 50 calls at seed `20261159`
had dK/dV repeat drift `0` and dQ drift `2.98023e-08`; the known-seed
`20260768` 2000-call race gate had dK/dV drift `0`, dQ drift
`3.35276e-08`, and no drift above `1e-6`.

Two independently seeded, fully device-synchronized 12-warmup/201-sample
rotations rejected the child:

| Seed | CuTe median/min/max us | parent median/min/max us | child median/min/max us | child / parent | child / CuTe |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `20261160` | `3145.668/3129.188/3383.460` | `4528.677/4510.662/4600.742` | `4547.462/4530.054/4617.574` | `1.004148` | `1.445627` |
| `20261161` | `3150.821/3128.133/3403.398` | `4527.720/4511.880/4648.296` | `4546.151/4532.136/4663.560` | `1.004071` | `1.442846` |

The hoist is therefore real but loses about `0.41%`, consistent with the
long-lived mapped address perturbing register allocation/scheduling more
than the three dynamically removed address operations save.  The child,
flag, and private binding were removed.  The clean rebuild
`/tmp/tk_fa4_safe_after_cached_dp_release_C.cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so`
has SHA-256
`8514509e19511a6fab31ec8d53b5d8682318fa08aac7a00b80fd8be225dc43f2`;
its exact H16 resource line is again REG `128`, STACK/LOCAL `0`, SHARED
`231276 B`.  A fresh 50-call control (seed `20261162`) was finite with exact
dK/dV and dQ repeat drift `2.98023e-08`.

##### True two-stage causal loop at S65536/H64: rejected

The matched NCU/SASS attribution resolves the apparent TMEM-load target. The
dominant TK sample reported on
`LDTM.16dp256bit.x8 ... tmem[+0x140]` is the first instruction after
`BAR.SYNC 5,288`; SourceCounters attributes the preceding collective wait to
that following instruction. It is not evidence of an independent dP-TMEM
address or load defect. Replacing the barrier would reopen the already-closed
score-fanout family, so no TMEM/barrier child was built.

The next measured open control site was the retained peeled route's
steady-state `ISETP.GE iteration, 0x2`. A private exact B1/S65536/H64 child
split only the eight-compute-warp q loop into a two-iteration causal prologue
and a dense main loop. Tensor, loader, reducer, semaphore, TMEM, MMA, and
output paths were unchanged. The expected dynamic saving was one comparison
per compute warp per steady score tile.

The static falsifier passed but exposed the cost. The retained parent's
complete instruction stream remained byte-identical to `d054f0b` (SHA-256
`f79ee5f9f9beef3d9de93d986c8dcc98061c26086158b267fa3d42d028ef59c6`).
Parent and child were REG `128`, STACK/LOCAL/spills `0`, SHARED `231276 B`,
with 52 `UTCHMMA.2CTA`. The child removed the exact hot
`ISETP.GE ... 0x2`, but cloning the compute body increased decoded
instructions `5320 -> 5808`, named `BAR.SYNC` sites `19 -> 27`, and
`WARPSYNC` sites `29 -> 35`.

Synchronized gates nevertheless established numerical safety:

| Gate | Result | CuTe-relative dQ/dK/dV rel-L2 |

family. Likewise, the apparent TK `LDTM ... tmem[+0x140]` hotspot is the

independent TMEM-address defect. Neither family was reopened.

##### Single-base branchless dO addressing at S65536/H64: retained

The retained branchless source route removed the local/peer load branch, but
its generic subtile implementation recomputed both swizzled addresses and
selected between them for each of four LDSM payloads. Matched NCU attributed
large added `VIADD`/`IMAD`/`LOP3` work to that address path.

The replacement has an exact layout proof. Both operands are BF16 subtiles
with 64 underlying rows and a 128-byte swizzle. They use the same
`source_row * 16`; the local operand differs only by `cta_rank * 64` columns,
which is one complete swizzle outer tile. The private child therefore computes
each operand's un-swizzled logical 16x64 base, selects that base once, and then
applies the same `row * 64 + col` offset and 128-byte swizzle for all four
loads. This is algebraically identical to `st_subtile::idx` and changes no
publication, payload, ownership, or barrier.

The retained parent body is byte-identical to the prior artifact (SHA-256
`fca4a5e3a04bde345d19309c412c6d56f8cbf09e93660ee2ae06fcf71a1377dc`).

gap and why the next scalable target is publication/barrier removal rather than
additional MMA or V-path work.

Schema v2 changes evidence semantics as follows:

- `gate_pass` remains the backward-compatible, mode-local gate;
- `correctness_pass`, `retention_pass`, `objective_evaluated`, and
  `objective_beats_cute` are independent fields;
- `overall_contract_pass` is the strict correctness plus CuTe objective, also
  requiring retention when a parent is timed;
- timing records a synchronized child-versus-CuTe correctness check before
  warmup/sampling; and
- repeat drift first triggers use the per-output limits (`dQ=2e-7`,
  `dK=dV=0`) rather than a hard-coded `1e-6` threshold.

negative path independently of the older `a4a90275...` selftest.

`588.416 us` CuTe (`1.21634x`), so it still clearly records a performance loss.

Stage A targets the measured V republication overhead without changing V
ownership or aliases. For the exact retained H8 flag set, each reducer already
loads its `32x128` V fragment once per owner, and `storage.ds` is V-only until
dP consumes it. Stage A therefore stores all four fragments and completes the
four-loader `v_local_ready` fan-in once per owner, using
`owner_pass & 1` rather than the frontier-forced `owner_phase=0`. It preserves
the cheap per-tile V token and `dp_operands_ready` count four.

The generic shared V stores are correctly ordered for the async-proxy dP MMA:
`group<8>::mm2_ABt` resolves to the SS overload in
`ThunderKittens/include/ops/thread/mma/tcgen05.cuh`, which unconditionally
emits `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta`. Exact child SASS shows the consumer
wait/acquire followed by `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA` at `0xc460`,
`FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` at `0xc470`, and the first dP `UTCHMMA.2CTA` at `0xc4f0`.
No redundant producer fence is required.

##### Cached FP32 split-2 bases with call-entry ordering: retained private objective win

Compared with the uncached BF16 binding, the new route additionally reuses the
internal FP32 base dK/dV allocations. Returned dQ and BF16 dK/dV outputs remain
per-call; the existing TLS cache continues to reuse preprocessing/dQ/frontier/
split scratch plus streams and events. The cache remains keyed by device,
owner stream, B/S/H, and exact FP32 tensor contracts. Public/default dispatch
is unchanged, and the private wrapper is guarded to exact B1/S1024/H8 or
B1/S4096/H1, causal, unpadded, nondeterministic inputs.

An order-sensitive validation exposed a real allocator/stream race in the
uncached control. Its temporary FP32 dK base and the following call's FP32 dQ
allocation are both 6 MiB at S1024/H8. The next call could reuse that block and
zero dQ on the auxiliary dQ stream before the previous caller-stream BF16
merge had consumed dK. The audited fix adds one disable-timing
`call_entry_ready` event to the TLS resources. At all three early auxiliary-dQ
sites, the caller records the event before current-call preprocessing and the
dQ stream waits before its first zero. This orders only prior caller-stream
work and preserves overlap between current preprocessing and dQ zeroing.

The matched profile confirmed that this H2 loss was wave underfill. TK used
64 CTAs, or 32 two-CTA clusters, for `0.42` waves/SM and spent `321-323 us`
in its integrated main. CuTe used 128 CTAs for `0.84` waves/SM and spent
`209 us` in main. Both used REG128 and no local memory; TK used 231,276 bytes
of shared memory versus CuTe's 224,256. NCU measured TK/CuTe warp instructions
at `30.730M/21.422M`, tensor-pipe activity at `14.64%/22.74%`, and
barrier/long-scoreboard/wait not-issued samples at
`3570/2577/726` versus `710/3715/413`. The dominant TK barrier PC remained
the already-closed score publication wait. The falsifiable next target was
therefore more concurrent useful cluster work rather than another local
score-barrier change.

An exact private owner-Q split now runs two copies of the balanced paired-K
schedule concurrently. Split 0 owns even Q tiles and split 1 owns odd Q
tiles. Both retain all K owners, write disjoint FP32 dK/dV partials, and
accumulate disjoint dQ tiles; one small kernel adds the two partials and
converts dK/dV to BF16. Three protocol corrections were required before the
route was valid: next-Q prefetch advances by the split stride, every role
carries the first owner's iteration parity into the second owner, and the
prefetch mbarrier separately carries its `N-1` transaction parity. The first
finite output then exposed that the causal mask used loop iteration instead
of the logical distance `q_tile_idx - 2*owner_idx`; correcting that coordinate
made the two rank diagonals element-correct.

The frozen artifact is 10,794,312 bytes at SHA-256
`b0845f3d46174184566f619ec5edfe6e8c53b8b97b6034da8622856d0c31acd1`.
The retained parent body is byte-identical at `3e782762...`; both split bodies
remain REG128, stack/local/spills zero, shared 231,276 bytes, and 52
`UTCHMMA.2CTA`. One-call seed `20269319`, 50-call seed `20269419`, and fixed
2000-call seed `20260768` passed. dQ/dK/dV relative-L2 errors were
`0.0034350/0.0037111/0.00018859`; dK/dV were repeat-exact and maximum dQ drift
was `2.235e-8`.
