##### S65536/H64 stats-warp score fanout: retained scheduling win

The later exact-shape chain reduced the qualified parent to 4,856
instructions while remaining REG128, STACK/LOCAL/spills 0, and using
232,444 shared bytes. Its final pre-fanout artifact is
`/tmp/_C_tk_bf16_bwd_s65536h64_v91_tma_v_score_k.so`, SHA-256
`989781a51217fe8ef89d05cf782189821c857b02f08a3231b35ef58b949b19fe`.
This parent couples the V TMA publication to the existing score-K
completion and measures about `223.1--223.5 ms`, versus about
`197.6--198.0 ms` for CuTe.

Three attempts to move work without changing the score handoff were
rejected first:

- V109 moved dK/dV output ownership to the compute warp and overlapped the
  stores with tensor-warp dQ work. Artifact
  `98ef5c3174030bdf0305916747873aab927ae60f998c191d7dc151ef2e909024`
  passed correctness but measured child/parent `1.0056608`, a 0.566%
  regression.

- V109b delayed that output path until the final dQ completion to more
  closely match CuTe. Artifact
  `b29d7e2a062b962651e23eab2eb9ae56fe081c223b32351179723d53225e917c`
  passed correctness but measured child/parent `1.0079327`, a 0.793%
  regression.

- V110 statically unrolled the reducer's fixed three-stage dQ drain.
  Artifact
  `34f09a2841d2c807caeda62961990284a4a37f2d7b6ba6b522e3e54c29737a86`
  passed correctness but measured child/parent `1.0342238`, a 3.422%
  regression.

V111 instead changes which already-active warp releases the score
dependency. In the parent, compute's 288-thread named barrier waits for
reducer warp 0, but reducer 0 first drains the previous dQ stage. The stats
warp has already prefetched and published the current LSE/dPsum values, so
the retained child lets that warp wait for `score_done` and join the
288-thread score barrier. Reducer 0 still consumes the same completion
independently but no longer delays compute's barrier. The math, data
movement, and barrier participant count are unchanged.

The retained artifact is
`/tmp/_C_tk_bf16_bwd_s65536h64_v111_stats_warp_score_fanout.so`, SHA-256
`83532286c43da212b9a7b56c0a5a1dff3aa1cbb95aa72ba7d6c161e15dc2be6c`,
size 12,538,640 bytes. It has 4,864 instructions versus the parent's 4,856,
and both remain REG128, STACK/LOCAL/spills 0, with 232,444 shared bytes.
The child moves the second score-barrier site from the reducer role to the
stats role.

One-call seed `2026073015` passed. A 50-call stress run at seed
`2026073024` also passed every call. Maximum repeated dQ/dK/dV drift was
`[5.960464477539063e-8,0,0]`; the first call versus CuTe had relative-L2
errors `[0.00269077,1.16239e-5,0]`, all within the established gates.

Two independent timing runs measured:

- 48 rotations, seed `2026073016`: parent `223101.110 us`, child
  `215250.384 us`, CuTe `197627.685 us`; child/parent `0.9648109`, a
  3.519% improvement.

- 96 rotations, seed `2026073017`: parent `223101.167 us`, child
  `215650.643 us`, CuTe `197974.265 us`; child/parent `0.9666047`, a
  3.340% improvement. The child won all 96 paired rotations; paired median
  ratio was `0.9686116` and median delta was `-7012.798 us`.

The source-level scheduler profile corroborates the timing. Eligible cycles
rise `16.12% -> 17.16%`, issued warps per scheduler rise `0.16 -> 0.17`,
no-eligible cycles fall `83.88% -> 82.84%`, and cycles per issued warp fall
`23.98 -> 22.50`. Total not-issued samples fall
`2,709,416 -> 2,675,448`; named-barrier samples fall
`1,195,741 -> 1,141,752`. The hottest compute score-barrier PC falls from
`801,049/855,728` not-issued/all samples to `746,310/797,629`. This is a
scheduling-latency win rather than an instruction-count reduction.

Two follow-ups delimit the useful part of the change:

- V112 attempted to expose LSE before dPsum with a separate shared-memory
  barrier, but activating the previously optimized-away object raised
  shared use to 232,460 bytes, 12 bytes over the device limit. Allocation-free
  V112b used a 288-thread named barrier instead. Artifact
  `dcf514eac6c13dca3f7bb4c42e5f9af799614e2c87e2765a92d675da216ff89a`
  passed correctness with no spills but measured child/parent
  `1.0263890`, a 2.639% regression.

- V113 removed four reducer score waits and made reducer 0 the sole
  dK-Q-completion waiter before the existing 384-thread barrier. Artifact
  `68eab3f60f509ab71903a00f7717b86e5a37fd10783c38adfaa7a9a6c10dfc2f`
  passed correctness and reduced static instructions `4864 -> 4848`.
  A 48-rotation run appeared 0.164% faster, but the independent 96-rotation
  run split wins exactly `48/96` and had paired median ratio `0.9999147`
  with median delta only `-18.577 us`. It was treated as neutral and
  removed.

At that checkpoint, only V111's stats-warp score fanout remained in the
exact private route. Against the 96-rotation CuTe result, its ratio was
`1.0892862`, or an 8.93% gap, down from the V91 parent's roughly 12.84%.

##### S65536/H64 batched dQ TMEM drain: retained lifetime win

V114 applies CuTe's useful dQ lifetime ordering without adopting the
previously rejected wide shared-memory reduction. Each reducer first issues
the three 32-column `LDTM.x32` loads for its 96-column dQ slice into three
register fragments. It then releases the aliased dQ/score TMEM immediately
and drains those fragments through the retained independent 32x32 reduction
streams. This separates TMEM lifetime shortening from reduction width and
removes the old per-chunk load/address/control loop from the dynamic path.

The retained private artifact is
`/tmp/_C_tk_bf16_bwd_s65536h64_v114_batched_dq_tmem_loads.so`, SHA-256
`ade863547c4328eb9eff03eced14b95b7d98537e2d71a50a5a59a5d0a81c102f`,
size 12,612,176 bytes. The exact child remains REG128 with
STACK/LOCAL/spills 0 and 232,444 shared bytes. Its decoded static body has
5,160 instructions versus V111's 4,864; the larger straight-line body
nevertheless eliminates repeated dynamic loop and address work.

One-call seed `2026073025` passed, including exact dK/dV agreement with
V111 and maximum dQ difference `5.960464477539063e-8`. A 50-call stress
run at seed `2026073028` passed every call with maximum repeated dQ/dK/dV
drift `[5.960464477539063e-8,0,0]` and remained within the established
CuTe gates.

Two independent timing runs measured:

- 48 rotations, seed `2026073026`: V114 `212464.806 us`, V111
  `215234.240 us`, CuTe `197726.844 us`; V114/V111 `0.9871329`, a
  1.287% improvement, and V114/CuTe `1.0745370`.

- 96 rotations, seed `2026073027`: V114 `212534.667 us`, V111
  `215069.083 us`, CuTe `198026.294 us`; V114/V111 `0.9882158`, a
  1.178% improvement, and V114/CuTe `1.0732649`, leaving a 7.33% gap.

The profile confirms both intended mechanisms. Issued instructions fall
from V111's `41.227B` to `39.922B` and executed instructions fall from
`41.135B` to `39.829B`, mainly through fewer `LOP3`, `ISETP`, `BRA`,
`IMAD`, `SYNCS`, and `S2R` instructions; `LDTM` and tensor-MMA counts are
unchanged. Named-barrier not-issued samples fall
`1,141,752 -> 1,016,306`, while the hottest compute score-barrier PC falls
`746,310 -> 606,085`.

V114 now issues fewer instructions than CuTe (`39.922B` versus `40.960B`)
but is still 7.33% slower. The remaining gap is therefore no longer an
aggregate instruction-count problem: V114 has about 3.0x CuTe's
named-barrier samples (`1.016M` versus `0.335M`), only `16.95%` eligible
cycles versus `19.78%`, and `22.78` cycles per issued warp versus `18.95`.
The next material step must reduce the 288-thread score-consumer barrier
topology rather than perform another address-only cleanup.

V114 is retained only in the exact private route. Public/default dispatch
remains unchanged. The installed module was not overwritten and remains
SHA-256
`201cfcdf051ecf702e15db825f8d214256502e1f4f2876b3a04725b9aa95744a`.

  `213031.085 us`, CuTe `198433.680 us`; V115/V114 `1.0012733`.

  `213222.779 us`, CuTe `198788.514 us`; V115/V114 `1.0022429`.

The paired barriers and independent waits move waiting among consumers but do

N128 dP destination into two non-aliased N64 stripes: the first used the
physical P columns 448--512 while score still occupied columns 320--448, and
the second used freed score columns 320--384 after score consumption. This
made the first dP stripe independent of score release, but the hardware
lowering required sixteen N64 dP MMAs instead of the retained eight N128

`UTCHMMA.2CTA` sites. Their modules are
`/tmp/_C_tk_bf16_bwd_s65536h64_v160_reverse_score_tmem_on_v148.so`

The cleaner control therefore still regresses by 0.297%. Reordering the

the producer's twelve-MMA score chain, not which ready score half is loaded
first. Both reverse-load implementations and their bindings were removed.

The fresh V148 profile and generated CuTe comparison now delimit both
remaining sites. The score fanout at relative PC `0x9330` represents the
completion of twelve serial K16 score MMAs; CuTe emits the same twelve K16
score MMAs, so there is no wider or omitted score payload to copy. Changing
fanout ownership/topology, descriptor cadence, partial-Q publication, or
independent dPsum work or score-load order has not advanced that completion.
Likewise, `dp_done` represents the fixed eight-MMA dP chain; compact issue
and commit forms change wrapper instructions but not its exposed tail. The
only non-aliased layout available inside the current persistent dK/dV/P TMEM
footprint fragments dP into N64 stripes and doubles its MMA count. A further
material reduction therefore requires a broader accumulator-lifetime or
ownership redesign that provides another contiguous N128 destination, rather
than another barrier or load-order rearrangement.

The child-only one-call launch failed at seed `20271532`; a launch-blocking
debug repeat at seed `20271536` failed at the same point. The bounded layout
audit found the structural mistake: dQ's 192 logical feature columns are
folded across four 32-row tensor-memory slices, and all four reducer warps
read the same three physical 32-column chunks. The next score MMA overwrites
all four slices, so the proposed early arrival from warps 2/3 created a real
read/write collision rather than releasing a disjoint tail. There is no
one-line safe release boundary in the retained layout.

synchronization rewrite or another compile. Public dispatch remains
unchanged. The installed module was restored byte-identically from the
retained S2048/H4 artifact at SHA-256
`201cfcdf051ecf702e15db825f8d214256502e1f4f2876b3a04725b9aa95744a`.

not-issued samples; later loads had materially lower stalls.

`fcdd85f08de1c834afb69dd2e0287e0fc9ae01d57cf002dfc9ad29a5be59ca4b`;

##### S65536/H64 consumer-only dV proxy fence: source-audit reject

A proposed private Exact512 child would have removed the normal-dO
generic-to-async proxy fence from all eight producer warps and relied on the
later BAR1 handoff plus tensor-side wait. The source proof fails: each
producer fence orders shared writes made by its executing warp, and neither
BAR1 nor a fence executed later by a different warp can publish those writes
on that producer's behalf. The valid warp-4-only fence move is already covered
by the Exact512 H128 experiment: warps 5--11 retained their producer fences,
warp 4 fenced after `BAR.SYNC`, and the measured child was slower. H64 uses
the same Exact512 machine specialization, so correcting this proposal would
duplicate that rejected experiment.

was removed. Clean retained hashes are kernel

binding

##### S65536/H64 retained peer TMA plus one local bulk copy: qualified parent win

The successful design preserves the original peer 64x64 dO TMA load. The
local feature half already occupies the correct row-half position when
`main.dout` is reinterpreted as the normal 128x64 dV operand. After dP
finishes, one elected lane therefore copies only the peer half from
`qdo.dout` into the unused half of `main.dout` with one 8-KiB shared bulk
copy. This removes the eight-warp register reshuffle without adding global
traffic.

The first correct version still had an all-warp completion wait before dS
publication and a CTA async-proxy fence before the copy. It passed one-call
seed `2026072832` and 50-call seed `2026072833`, but timing seed
`2026072834` measured child `263131.940 us` versus parent `262836.501 us`,
or `1.0011240410`, so that version was not retained.

The final minimized version removes both operations. The proof is structural:
`qdo.q0` and `qdo.q1` occupy the first 16 KiB of the union, while
`qdo.dout` occupies the final 8 KiB at offset 16 KiB. Later dS publication
aliases only the first 16 KiB and cannot overwrite the dO copy source.
Furthermore, the source is written by a completed TMA transaction and read by
the shared bulk engine, so no generic-to-async proxy handoff is required.

Static extraction gives the exact retained parent machine-word SHA-256
`ab7fead4ad07dde13e86ac720dfa5d550a5318a5341681f8bdc2b0ff97e5e232`
and child
`6b98ad3cdff91fddab33e10bee4ba5c9f8f34b69253eac7e440ddc6a4caaf629`.

shared bytes with no spills. The child preserves all 52 `UTCHMMA.2CTA`, 24
`UTMALDG.5D`, 17 LDTM, four STTM, 128 exp2 and 256 BF16-pack instructions.
It changes LDSM `4 -> 0`, STSM `36 -> 32`, named-barrier waits `19 -> 17`,
barrier arrivals `4 -> 3`, warp syncs `26 -> 25`, and shared bulk copies
`1 -> 2`.

One-call seed `2026072835`, 50-call seed `2026072836`, and all 2,000 calls at
fixed seed `20260768` pass. Maximum repeated dQ/dK/dV drift is
`[8.940696716308594e-8,0,0]`.

##### S65536/H64 CuTe schedule port: three retained exact-shape wins

A fresh audit of
`flash-attention/flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd_sm100.py` corrected one earlier
overstatement. For two-CTA D192, CuTe aliases the Q and Qt pipeline state and
shared allocation, but it still issues distinct `load_Q` and `load_Qt` TMA
transactions because their CTA-local partitions differ. TK's score-Q and
dK-Q partitions overlap only half their elements, so one transaction cannot
legally serve both views. The portable strategy is sequential stage reuse,
loader ownership, packed score arithmetic, and operand lifetime management,
not zero-copy reinterpretation.

The first exact B1/S65536/H64 child moves the second wide dK-Q publication
from reducer warp 0 to loader warp 13. The initial Q/dO publication is peeled
before the loader loop, then the loop carries its current completion pointer
and phase. This preserves the two distinct Q transactions while shortening
the reducer's polling/control path. Its machine-word SHA-256 is
`09cbba00eb44f75c839925e1bbd14e4e6e4e107d31409dae656dbd21403ab3ae`;
it has 5,496 instructions, REG128, STACK/LOCAL/spills 0, 231,276 total shared
bytes, 52 `UTCHMMA.2CTA`, and 31 static `UTMALDG.5D` sites.

`-37,705,245`, and `ISETP.GE` `-33,685,504`.

The second child adopts CuTe's packed score transform. It places score
